One personally cultivates the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; teaches others to cultivate the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; praises the dharmas of the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; and also joyfully commends those who cultivate the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

Having personally entered the eight liberations, he teaches others to enter the eight liberations, praises the dharma of the eight liberations, and also joyfully extols those who have entered the eight liberations.

Having personally entered the nine successive meditative attainments, he teaches others to enter the nine successive meditative attainments, praises the dharma of the nine successive meditative attainments, and also joyfully extols those who have entered the nine successive meditative attainments.

The same applies to his self-cultivation of the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered knowledges, great loving-kindness and great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities.

One practices the dharma of being free from error oneself and practices the dharma of constant relinquishment oneself; one teaches others to practice the dharma of being free from error and the dharma of constant relinquishment; one praises the dharma of being free from error and the dharma of constant relinquishment; and one also joyfully commends those who practice the dharma of being free from error and the dharma of constant relinquishment.
One personally attains all-knowledge, teaches others to attain all-knowledge, praises the dharma of all-knowledge, and also joyfully extols those who have attained all-knowledge.
When this bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās, having shared all their giving with sentient beings, they dedicate it toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi by way of non-apprehension.

Having shared all their morality, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom with all sentient beings, they dedicate these toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, because of the principle of non-apprehension.
When these good sons and good daughters practice the six pāramitās in this way, they form this thought:

"If I do not practice giving, I shall be born into a poor family; I will be unable to bring sentient beings to maturity or purify the Buddha-lands, nor will I be able to attain all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā)."

If I do not maintain the precepts, I shall be reborn among the three evil realms; I will not even attain a human body, let alone be able to bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-lands, or attain all-knowledge.

If I do not cultivate patience, my sense faculties will be impaired and my physical form will be incomplete; I shall be unable to attain the bodhisattva’s perfect body, through the sight of which sentient beings would inevitably reach *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Furthermore, I would be unable to use that perfect body to bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and attain all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
If I were to be indolent, I would be unable to attain the path of a bodhisattva, nor would I be able to accomplish the maturation of sentient beings, purify the buddha-field, or attain all-knowledge.

If my mind were distracted, I would be unable to give birth to the various dhyānas and samādhis; without these dhyānas and samādhis, I could not bring sentient beings to maturity, purify Buddha-lands, or attain all-knowledge.

If I were without wisdom, I would be unable to attain the wisdom of skillful means; by means of the wisdom of skillful means, I transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, and attain all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).
This bodhisattva further reflects in this way:
"I must not, out of following stinginess and greed, fail to fulfill the dāna-pāramitā.
I must not, out of following the violation of precepts, fail to fulfill the śīla-pāramitā."
One should not, out of following anger and hatred, fail to fulfill the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā).
One should not, out of following indolence, fail to fulfill the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā).
One should not, due to following a distracted mind, fail to fulfill the dhyāna-pāramitā.
One should not, due to following a deluded mind, fail to fulfill the prajñā-pāramitā.

If I were not fully endowed with the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom, I would ultimately never be able to remain inseparable from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*) and attain these merits of this life and future lives.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! How rare!”
"This Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is for the sake of dedicating [merit] toward the mind of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), and also for the sake of not giving rise to a conceited mind.
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: "Kauśika!"
"How is it that the prajñāpāramitā of a bodhisattva mahāsattva serves both to dedicate toward the mind of sarvajñā (all-knowledge) and to prevent the arising of pride?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), they bestow gifts upon the Buddhas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, as well as the poor, the destitute, beggars, and travelers on the road.
Because this bodhisattva lacks skillful means, they give rise to a sense of superiority.
If they practice the mundane perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), they say:
"I am practicing the perfection of ethical discipline; I am able to fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline."
Because they lack skillful means, they give rise to a haughty mind and say:
"I practice the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, and the perfection of meditation; I practice the perfection of wisdom; I cultivate the perfection of wisdom."
"Because this worldly *prajñāpāramitā* lacks skillful means (*upāya*), they give rise to a conceited mind.
World-Honored One!
When a bodhisattva cultivates the worldly four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), they think to themselves:"
"I practice the four foundations of mindfulness; I am fully endowed with the four foundations of mindfulness.
Because he lacks the power of skillful means, he gives rise to a haughty mind.
"I practice the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path."
He thought to himself:
"I shall cultivate the three samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
By cultivating all gates of samādhi, I shall attain all gates of dhāraṇī."

I shall cultivate the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique dharmas; I shall bring sentient beings to maturity, I shall purify the Buddha-lands, and I shall attain all-knowledge.
"Because they are attached to a self and lack the power of skillful means, they give rise to a sense of superiority.
World-Honored One!
Thus, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices worldly wholesome dharmas, because of attachment to a self, they give rise to a sense of superiority."
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices supramundane dānapāramitā, they do not apprehend a giver, they do not apprehend a recipient, and they do not apprehend the gift.”
In this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the supramundane perfection of giving;
for the sake of dedicating it toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he likewise does not give rise to a conceited mind.
When practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), ethical discipline is not apprehended.
When practicing the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), patience is not apprehended.
When practicing the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), vigor is not apprehended.
One practices the dhyāna-pāramitā, yet dhyāna is unattainable.
One practices the prajñā-pāramitā, yet prajñā is unattainable.
One cultivates the four foundations of mindfulness, yet the four foundations of mindfulness are unattainable.
Up to and including the cultivation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, those eighteen unique qualities are unattainable.
One cultivates great loving-kindness and great compassion, yet great loving-kindness and great compassion are unattainable.
"Up to and including the cultivation of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), all-knowledge itself is unattainable.
World-Honored One!
Thus, this Prajñāpāramitā of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is for the sake of dedicating [merit] toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and also for the sake of not giving rise to a haughty mind."
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Eight;
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of Kucha during the Later Qin Dynasty.
Chapter 32: The Chapter on the Great Clarification (The Chapter on the Jeweled Stupa in the Dan edition).
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra-devānām-indra, saying:

"If there are good men or good women who hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, draw near to it, read and recite it, and maintain right mindfulness—never departing from the mind of *sarvajñatā*—then when two armies are at war, because these good men or good women recite the *prajñāpāramitā*, they shall never lose their lives upon entering the ranks of battle, nor shall they be wounded by swords or arrows."

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family have for a long night practiced the six pāramitās; they have removed for themselves the sword and arrow of lustful desire, and have also removed the sword and arrow of lustful desire for others;
they have removed for themselves the sword and arrow of anger, and have also removed the sword and arrow of anger for others.
One removes for oneself the sword and arrow of ignorance, and also removes for others the sword and arrow of ignorance;
one removes for oneself the sword and arrow of wrong views, and also removes for others the sword and arrow of wrong views;
one removes for oneself the sword and arrow of the fetters and defilements, and also removes for others the sword and arrow of the fetters and defilements.
Having personally removed the swords and arrows of the fetters and afflictions, they also remove the swords and arrows of the fetters and afflictions of others. Kausika!
By this cause and condition, these sons and daughters of good family shall not be wounded by swords or arrows.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

When these sons of good family or daughters of good family hear this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they receive, uphold, draw near to, read, recite, and correctly contemplate it, never departing from the mind of sarvajña (omniscience)."

Whether by fumigating with poisonous drugs, by means of sorcery, by fire-pits, by deep waters, by wishing to kill with a blade, or by giving them poison—none of these various evils can cause them harm.
Why is this? This Prajñāpāramitā is the great mantra of illumination; it is the unsurpassed mantra of illumination.
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family studies within this mantra of illumination, they will not afflict themselves, nor will they afflict others, nor will they afflict both.

Why is this? Because these good men and good women do not apprehend a self, do not apprehend sentient beings, do not apprehend a life span, and so on, up to the knower and the seer—all of which are unapprehendable.
One cannot apprehend form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor can one apprehend even the knowledge of all modes.
Because they cannot be apprehended, one does not afflict oneself, nor does one afflict others, nor does one afflict both.

Because this study is a great mantra of illumination, one attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and observes the minds of all sentient beings to preach the Dharma according to their inclinations. Why is this?

The Buddhas of the past studied this great vidyā-mantra and attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; the Buddhas of the future will study this great vidyā-mantra and shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; the Buddhas of the present study this great vidyā-mantra and attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, if one merely transcribes the Prajñāpāramitā into a volume and makes offerings to it in one's home, even if one does not accept, read, recite, explain, or correctly attend to it, neither humans nor non-humans shall be able to find an opportunity to cause harm in that place."

Why is this? Because this Prajñāpāramitā is protected by the gods of the Four Great Kings throughout the trichiliocosm, up to the sons of the gods in the Akaniṣṭha heaven, as well as by the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven in immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya worlds throughout the ten directions.
This is the dwelling place of the Prajñāpāramitā; all the devas come to it to offer worship, reverence, respect, praise, and prostrations before departing.

If these sons or daughters of good family merely transcribe the Prajñāpāramitā within or without their houses, beneath a *śirīṣa* tree, even if humans or non-humans should approach with malicious intent, they will be unable to find an opportunity to harm them.

Why is this? It is because in this place the Buddhas of the past attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and the Buddhas of the future and the Buddhas of the present likewise attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* therein.

Having attained Buddhahood, he bestows fearlessness and intrepidity upon all sentient beings, causing immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* numbers of beings to receive the blessings and joys of the heavens and the human realm, and likewise causing immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* numbers of beings to attain the fruit of *srotāpanna*, up to and including *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
By the power of the *prajñāpāramitā*, one receives honor, prostrations, and offerings of flowers, incense, garlands, powdered incense, fragrant oils, banners, canopies, and music in this place.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes out the Prajñāpāramitā and makes offerings to it with flowers, incense, necklaces, and even musical performances;”

If there is someone who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, makes offerings to his relics, or erects stupas to offer them with worship, reverence, respect, and praise, using flowers, incense, garlands, and even musical performances as offerings.
"Of these two, which one would obtain greater merit?
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra, "I shall question you in return; answer me according to your own understanding."

What do you think: as for the Buddha’s attainment of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and the acquisition of this body, from which path did he train to attain this all-knowledge and acquire this body?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The Buddha has learned from the study of the *prajñāpāramitā* to attain all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) as well as the body endowed with the marks and signs.
The Buddha told Śakra Devānām Indra:
"So it is, so it is, Kauśika! It is from training in the *prajñāpāramitā* that the Buddha has attained all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*)."

Kauśika! It is not by virtue of the body endowed with the marks and signs that one is called a Buddha; it is because of the attainment of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā) that one is called a Buddha. Kauśika!
This Buddha’s knowledge of all modes arises from the perfection of wisdom.
For this reason, Kauśika, this body of the Buddha is the locus upon which the knowledge of all modes relies; it is by means of this body that the Buddha attains the knowledge of all modes.
"Good son! You should reflect in this way:
'This body is the locus upon which all-encompassing wisdom (sarvākārajñatā) relies.'"
"Therefore, after my parinirvāṇa, my relics shall receive offerings.

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family hears this Prajñāpāramitā, writes it down, receives and maintains it, draws near to it, reads and recites it, and correctly contemplates it; and if they honor, worship, respect, and praise it with flowers, incense, garlands, powdered incense, fragrant oils, banners, canopies, and music."
These sons and daughters of good family will thereby be making offerings to the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā). For this reason, Kauśika,

if any son or daughter of good family writes down this Prajñāpāramitā, or receives, upholds, approaches, reads, recites, explains, and correctly contemplates it, and honors, respects, praises, and makes offerings to it with flowers, incense, garlands, and even musical performances— [they shall obtain great merit].
This person gains much merit. Why is this?

It is because within this Prajñāpāramitā the five pāramitās are born; from it are born the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence, the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and all samādhis, all dhyānas, and all dhāraṇī-doors—all are born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
The maturation of sentient beings and the purification of Buddha-fields both arise from the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

The bodhisattva’s accomplishment of the physical form, the accomplishment of the necessities of life, the accomplishment of retinues, and the accomplishment of great loving-kindness and great compassion—all these arise from the perfection of wisdom.
The great clans of Kṣatriyas, the great clans of Brāhmaṇas, and the great households of householders are all born from the Prajñāpāramitā.

From the Heaven of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; from the Srotāpanna up to the Arhat, the Pratyekabuddha, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the Buddhas, and the all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā) of the Buddhas—all are born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If the people of Jambudvīpa do not make offerings to this Prajñāpāramitā, nor revere, respect, or praise it, is it because they do not know that making offerings brings about great benefit?”
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
“Kauśika, what do you think?
How many people in Jambudvīpa have unshakable faith in the Buddha, and unshakable faith in the Dharma and the Saṅgha?”
How many people have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha?
How many people have attained definitive understanding of the Buddha, and have attained definitive understanding of the Dharma and the Saṅgha?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Few are the people of Jambudvīpa who have attained indestructible faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; few, too, are those who are free from doubt and possess definitive understanding regarding the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.”
“Kauśika! What do you think?

How many people in Jambudvīpa have attained the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three gates of liberation, the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, the four unhindered knowledges, and the six supernormal powers?”
How many people in Jambudvīpa, by severing the three fetters, attain the stage of Srotāpanna?
How many people, by severing the three fetters and further attenuating lust, hatred, and delusion, attain the stage of Sakṛdāgāmin?
How many people have severed the five lower fetters and attained the path of the Non-returner (anāgāmin)?
How many people have severed the five higher fetters and attained the path of the Arhat?
How many people in Jambudvīpa seek the state of a Pratyekabuddha?
"How many people have resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
Śakra-devānām-indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
In Jambudvīpa, few people attain the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; indeed, even fewer people resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra: “So it is, so it is! Kauśika!”

Few are those whose faith in the Buddha is indestructible, whose faith in the Dharma is indestructible, and whose faith in the Saṅgha is indestructible; few are those who have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṅgha; few are those who have reached a definitive understanding of the Buddha, a definitive understanding of the Dharma, and a definitive understanding of the Saṅgha.

Kauśika! Furthermore, there are few people who attain the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three gates of liberation, the eight liberations, the nine successive concentrations, the four unhindered knowledges, and the six supernormal powers.

Kauśika! Furthermore, few people sever the three fetters and attain the stage of Srotāpanna; few sever the three fetters and, with the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, attain the stage of Sakṛdāgāmin; few sever the five lower fetters and attain the stage of Anāgāmin; and few sever the five higher fetters and attain the stage of Arhat.

Few are those who seek the state of a pratyekabuddha; among them, even fewer are those who resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; and among those who have resolved their minds, even fewer are those who practice the bodhisattva path.

Why is this? Because these sentient beings, in previous lives, did not see the Buddha, did not hear the Dharma, and did not make offerings to the Sangha of bhikṣus; they did not practice giving, did not maintain the precepts, were not patient, were not diligent, did not cultivate meditative concentration, and did not possess wisdom. They did not hear of internal emptiness, external emptiness, up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence; nor did they hear of or cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Furthermore, they did not hear of or cultivate the various gates of samādhi or the various gates of dhāraṇī, nor did they cultivate all-knowledge or the knowledge of all modes.

Kauśika! For this reason, you should know that there are but few sentient beings whose faith in the Buddha is indestructible, whose faith in the Dharma is indestructible, and whose faith in the Saṅgha is indestructible; even fewer than these seek the path of a pratyekabuddha; among them, even fewer give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; among those who have given rise to such a mind, even fewer practice the bodhisattva path; and among those, even fewer attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Kauśika! With my Buddha-eye, I see immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings in the eastern direction who have resolved their minds and practice the path of a bodhisattva for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Because these sentient beings are far removed from the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) of the *prajñā-pāramitā*, only one or two abide in the stage of *avaivartika*, while the majority fall into the stages of *śrāvaka* or *pratyekabuddha*.
It is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions,
and above and below. For this reason, Kauśika,

a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has resolved their mind toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* should hear the *prajñāpāramitā*, and should receive, uphold, draw near to, recite, explain, and correctly contemplate it.

Having received, upheld, approached, recited, explained, and correctly recollected it, one should write out the sūtra scrolls and reverently make offerings to them, honoring, respecting, and praising them with flowers, incense, garlands, and even musical performances.
As for all other wholesome dharmas that enter into the Prajñāpāramitā, these too should be heard, accepted, maintained, and even correctly recollected.
What are these other wholesome dharmas?

That is to say: the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, and the perfection of meditation; the emptiness of the internal, the emptiness of the external, up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence; the various gates of samādhi and the various gates of dhāraṇī; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; and great loving-kindness and great compassion.
All such immeasurable wholesome dharmas as these enter into the Prajñāpāramitā; these, too, should be heard, received, upheld, and even correctly recollected.
Why is this? These sons and daughters of good family should reflect in this way:

"When the Buddha was originally a bodhisattva, he practiced and studied in this manner—namely, the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity; from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence; the various gateways of samādhi and the various gateways of dhāraṇī; the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha, and great loving-kindness and great compassion."
We should likewise study these immeasurable dharmas of the Buddhas.
Why is this? Because the Prajñāpāramitā is what we revere, and the Dhyānapāramitā, as well as all other immeasurable wholesome dharmas, are also what we revere.
This is the Dharma-seal of all Buddhas; it is the Dharma-seal of all Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, Anāgāmins, Sakṛdāgāmins, and Srotāpannas.

All Buddhas train in this Prajñāpāramitā up to and including all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and thereby attain the further shore; likewise, Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, Anāgāmins, Sakṛdāgāmins, and Srotāpannas also train in this Prajñāpāramitā up to and including all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) and thereby attain the further shore.
"For this reason, Kauśika!

Whether the Buddha is in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa, a son of good family or a daughter of good family should rely upon the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), the perfection of meditation (dhyānapāramitā), the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā), the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā), the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), and the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā); they should likewise rely upon everything up to all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā)."

Why is this? Because this Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), is that upon which all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and all the worldlings—gods, humans, and asuras—may rely.

Kauśika! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, after the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, construct a stūpa of the seven precious substances one yojana in height, and with celestial incense, celestial flowers, celestial garlands, celestial powdered incense, celestial unguents, celestial robes, celestial banners and canopies, and celestial music, they make offerings, pay homage, revere, and praise it.
“Kauśika! What do you think? Would that son or daughter of good family gain much merit by reason of this?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied:
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so, it is very much so!
The Buddha said:

"It is not as good as if these sons and daughters of good family hear this Prajñāpāramitā, write it down, receive and uphold it, draw near to it, correctly contemplate it, and do not depart from the mind of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), while also revering, honoring, and praising it with offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, unguents, banners, canopies, and music."
"The merit of these good sons and good daughters will be great.
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"Set aside the case of a single stūpa made of the seven treasures."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, were to erect throughout Jambudvīpa after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa stūpas made of the seven precious substances, each one yojana in height, and were to honor, respect, and praise them, making offerings of incense, flowers, garlands, banners, canopies, and musical performances;
"Kauśika! What do you think? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied:
“World-Honored One!
That merit would be exceedingly great.
The Buddha said:
"It is not as meritorious as the merit of these sons and daughters of good family who, as previously described, make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā.
Kausika! Furthermore, let alone a single Jambudvīpa filled with stupas made of the seven treasures."

Suppose there are sons or daughters of good family who, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, erect stupas made of the seven precious substances after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa—filling the four continents, each one yojana in height—and make offerings to them as previously described.
"Kauśika! What do you think? Would that son or daughter of good family have much merit?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied:
"Very much, very much," [they replied].
The Buddha said:

"It is not as great as the merit of these sons and daughters of good family who write down and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, and who honor, respect, praise, and make offerings to it with flowers, incense, and even music; their merit is far greater."
Kauśika! Let us set aside the case of filling the four continents with stupas made of the seven treasures.

Suppose there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, erects stupas made of the seven treasures—each one yojana in height—throughout an entire small chiliocosm after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and makes offerings to them as previously described.
"Kauśika, what do you think? Would that son or daughter of good family have much merit?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied:
“It is very much so,” the Buddha said.

“It is not equal to the merit of these sons and daughters of good family who write down this Prajñāpāramitā, and who receive, uphold, revere, honor, and praise it, making offerings of flowers, incense, and even music; their merit is far greater.”
Kauśika! Let us set aside the case of small thousandfold world-systems filled with stupas made of the seven precious substances.

Suppose there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, erects stupas made of the seven precious substances—each one yojana in height—in as many medium two-thousandfold world-systems as there are in those [small] systems, after the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, and makes offerings to them as before.
Therefore, making offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā brings far greater merit.
Furthermore, setting aside the seven-jeweled stūpas in two thousand intermediate lands,
suppose there were a son of good family or a daughter of good family who made offerings of celestial flowers, celestial incense, celestial garlands, and even celestial music.
"What do you think, Śakra Devānām-indra? Would that son or daughter of good family acquire much merit?
Śakra Devānām-indra replied, "World-Honored One!"
"Very much, very much!

The Buddha said, "It is not as great as the merit of these sons and daughters of good family who write down this Prajñāpāramitā, receive, uphold, revere, respect, and praise it, and make offerings to it with incense, flowers, and even music; their merit is far greater."
Furthermore, setting aside the seven-jeweled stūpas within the trichiliocosm,

suppose every single sentient being within that trichiliocosm, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, were each to erect a seven-jeweled stūpa after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and to offer worship, respect, praise, flowers, incense, and even music.

If there are good sons or good daughters who write down and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, and even go so far as to maintain right mindfulness of it without departing from the mind of *sarvajñatā* (omniscience), and furthermore honor, revere, praise, and make offerings to it with flowers, incense, garlands, and even music, these people will obtain exceedingly great merit.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying: “So it is, so it is!
World-Honored One!”
If a person makes offerings to, reveres, honors, and praises this Prajñāpāramitā, they are making offerings to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
“World-Honored One!

If all sentient beings in as many lands in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River were each to make offerings to the Buddha, and after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, were each to erect a stupa made of the seven precious substances one yojana in height;”
If such a person were to honor, revere, and praise them for an eon, or even slightly less than an eon, making offerings of flowers, incense, and even music— World-Honored One!
“Would these sons or daughters of good family acquire much merit?
The Buddha said, “Very much.”
Śakra Devānām Indra said:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who write down and uphold this Prajñāpāramitā, and even correctly bring it to mind, and furthermore honor, revere, and praise it, making offerings of flowers, incense, and even music, their merit will be exceedingly great."
Why is this? World-Honored One!
All wholesome dharmas enter into the Prajñāpāramitā, namely the ten paths of wholesome action, the four... [and so forth].
The dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds, the four formless attainments, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment,
the three gates of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— the four truths— the truth of suffering, the truth of origination,
the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path— the six supernormal powers, the eight liberations, and the nine successive attainments.
The perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom;
from internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence; the various gates of samādhi and the various gates of dhāraṇī; and the ten [powers] of a Buddha.
The powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered knowledges, great loving-kindness and great compassion,
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the knowledge of all things, the knowledge of the paths, and the knowledge of all modes.
“World-Honored One!
This is called the Dharma-seal of all Buddhas.
Within this Dharma, all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, as well as all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, study this Dharma and thereby attain the further shore.”

33. Chapter on the Accomplishment of the Exposition, Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-Three on the Accomplishment of the Exposition. At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: “So it is, so it is!”

Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family who write down, uphold, study, approach, read, recite, explain, and correctly contemplate this Prajñāpāramitā sūtra, and furthermore honor it with flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, fragrant oils, banners, canopies, and music, shall obtain immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless merit.
Why is this? All the Buddhas' omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*) are born from the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

The bodhisattva mahāsattvas' perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*), perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), and perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*) are all born from the perfection of wisdom.

From the emptiness of the internal up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence, and from the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all are born from the perfection of wisdom.
The five eyes of all Buddhas are born from the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

The maturation of sentient beings, the purification of Buddha-fields, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), and the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*)—all the qualities of a Buddha are born from the perfection of wisdom.
The vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and the vehicle of the buddhas all arise from the perfection of wisdom.
For this reason, Kauśika!

If good sons or good daughters write down, uphold, draw near to, read, recite, explain, and correctly contemplate this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and further make offerings to it with flowers, incense, and so forth, even up to [the finest offerings].
Why is this? Kauśika!
If the Prajñāpāramitā remains in the world, the Jewel of the Buddha, the Jewel of the Dharma, and the Jewel of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus will never perish.

If the Prajñāpāramitā exists in the world, then the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless absorptions, the pāramitās from dāna-pāramitā up to prajñā-pāramitā, the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, omniscience (sarvajñatā), and the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) will all appear in the world.

If the Prajñāpāramitā exists in the world, then there will be in the world the great clans of Kṣatriyas, the great clans of Brāhmaṇas, and the great families of householders; the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven; the fruits of Srotāpanna up to Arhatship; the path of the Pratyekabuddha; the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; and the unsurpassed path of the Buddha—including the turning of the wheel of Dharma, the maturing of sentient beings, and the purification of Buddha-fields.

Chapter 34: Encouraging Retention The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-Four: Encouraging Retention At that time, all the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven in this trichiliocosm addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"One should receive this Prajñāpāramitā; one should uphold it, draw near to it, read and recite it, explain it, and maintain right mindfulness of it."

Why is this? Because by upholding the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintaining right mindfulness of it, all the wholesome dharmas one has cultivated and accumulated shall be fully perfected; the hosts of devas will increase, and the asuras will diminish.

Because these sons of the gods uphold the Prajñāpāramitā and maintain right mindfulness of it, the lineage of the Buddha will not be interrupted, nor will the lineages of the Dharma and the Saṃgha be interrupted.

Because the lineage of the Buddha, the lineage of the Dharma, and the lineage of the Saṅgha are not severed, the pāramitā of giving (dāna), the pāramitā of ethical discipline (śīla), the pāramitā of patience (kṣānti), the pāramitā of vigor (vīrya), the pāramitā of meditation (dhyāna), and the pāramitā of wisdom (prajñā) all appear in the world.
The four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, as well as the bodhisattva path, all appear in the world.

The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of arhatship, the path of the pratyekabuddha, and the path of the Buddha—all from the stream-enterer up to the Buddha—appear in the world.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: "Kauśika,
you should receive this Prajñāpāramitā, uphold it, read and recite it, explain it, and maintain right mindfulness of it."
Why is this? If the asuras should give rise to the thought of wishing to fight with the gods of the Thirty-three Heavens, Kausika!
At that time, you should recite and contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā; then the evil intentions of the asuras will immediately be extinguished and will not arise again. Kausika!
If the five signs of death appear for any sons or daughters of the gods, they are destined to fall into unfavorable states.
You should recite the Prajñāpāramitā before them.
Because these sons and daughters of the gods have heard the merits of the Prajñāpāramitā, they will return to their original abodes.
Why is this? Because hearing the Prajñāpāramitā brings great benefit. Furthermore, Kauśika!
If there are good men or good women, or sons or daughters of the gods, who hear this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra with their ears,
by virtue of this merit, they shall gradually attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Why is this? Kausika!
All the Buddhas of the past and their disciples studied this Prajñāpāramitā, thereby attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and entering nirvana without remainder.

Kauśika! All Buddhas of future ages, all Buddhas of the present in the ten directions, and their disciples, have all studied this Prajñāpāramitā, thereby attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and entering nirvana without remainder.
Why is this? Kauśika!
This Prajñāpāramitā encompasses all wholesome dharmas—whether they be the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of buddhas.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Prajñāpāramitā is the great vidyā-mantra, the unsurpassed vidyā-mantra, the peerless vidyā-mantra.”
For what reason?
World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is able to eliminate all that is unwholesome and is able to bestow all wholesome dharmas.
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra: “So it is, so it is! Kauśika!”
The Prajñāpāramitā is the great vidyā-mantra, the unsurpassed vidyā-mantra,
the unequaled vidyā-mantra.
Why is this so, Kauśika?
Because of this vidyā-mantra, the Buddhas of the past attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
the Buddhas of the future and the Buddhas of the ten directions in the present world also, by means of this vidyā-mantra, attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Because of this vidyā-mantra, there come to be in the world the ten paths of wholesome action; there come to be the four dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds, and the four formless attainments; there come to be the pāramitā of dāna up to the pāramitā of prajñā; there come to be the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; there come to be the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), suchness (tathatā), the mark of phenomena (dharmalakṣaṇa), the stability of phenomena (dharmaniyāmatā), the fixed course of phenomena (dharmasthititā), and the reality limit (bhūtakoṭi); there come to be the five eyes, the fruit of srotāpanna up to the fruit of arhat, the path of the pratyekabuddha, all-knowledge (sarvajñatā), and the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).
Kauśika! It is because of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that the ten wholesome paths arise in the world.
It is because of them that the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, up to all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), and from the stream-enterer (srotāpanna) up to all the Buddhas, appear in the world.
Just as when the full moon shines with illumination, the constellations are also able to shine with illumination; so it is, Kauśika!

All the wholesome dharmas and true dharmas of the world, from the ten wholesome paths of action up to the knowledge of all modes, arise from the bodhisattva whenever the Buddhas do not appear in the world.
This skillful means (*upāya-bala*) of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva arises entirely from the *prajñāpāramitā*.

By means of this skillful means, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the *dānapāramitā* up to the *dhyānapāramitā*, the emptiness of the internal (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) up to the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*). Without realizing the stages of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, they are also able to bring sentient beings to maturity, purify buddha-fields, achieve the perfection of lifespan, the perfection of the buddha-field, and the perfection of the bodhisattva retinue, and attain all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*)—all of which arise from the *prajñāpāramitā*.

"Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family hears this Prajñāpāramitā, receives and upholds it, draws near to it, and even maintains right mindfulness of it, that person shall attain the accomplishment of merits in both the present life and future lives."
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One,
what are the merits in this present life that a son of good family or a daughter of good family obtains by upholding the Prajñāpāramitā, and so forth, up to correctly recollecting it?”
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā, they shall never die from poison, shall not be wounded by weapons, shall not be harmed by water or fire, and shall not be afflicted by the four hundred and four diseases;
this excludes only the retribution of their past-life karma."

"Furthermore, Kauśika! If any official legal matter should arise, because this son or daughter of good family has read and recited this Prajñāpāramitā, when they go before the authorities, no one will be able to reproach them."
Why is this? It is because of the majestic power of this Prajñāpāramitā.
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family recites this Prajñāpāramitā and goes before a king, or before a prince, or before a great minister.
The king, the crown prince, and the ministers were all filled with joy; they inquired after one another’s well-being and conversed with harmonious minds. Why was this?
Because these sons and daughters of good family constantly possess loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, and their hearts are directed toward all sentient beings.

Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family upholds the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintains it with correct mindfulness, they shall obtain these various kinds of merits in this present life.
Kauśika! What are the merits that these sons and daughters of good family obtain in future lives?

These sons and daughters of good family shall never be separated from the ten paths of wholesome action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds, the four formless attainments, the six pāramitās, the four foundations of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Such a person shall never fall into the three evil realms, and their physical form will be complete.
They shall never be born into poverty or lowliness, nor as a craftsman, a scavenger, or a carrier of corpses.
They shall constantly possess the thirty-two marks and always attain birth by transformation, being born in the various present Buddha-fields.

They shall never be separated from the supernormal powers of a bodhisattva; if they wish to go from one Buddha-field to another to make offerings to the Buddhas and listen to their teachings, they shall immediately be able to travel to whichever Buddha-field they desire.
They are able to bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields,
gradually attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Kausika!
This is called the merit for future lives.

For this reason, Kauśika, sons of good family and daughters of good family should receive, uphold, draw near to, read, recite, explain, and correctly attend to this Prajñāpāramitā; they should offer it worship with flowers, incense, and even music, and never depart from the mind of *sarvajñatā* (omniscience).
These good men and good women shall, up until their attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, achieve the fulfillment of merits in both this life and future lives.
Chapter 35: On Sending Away the Diverse (The Brahmin Chapter). At that time, various non-Buddhist practitioners and brahmins came to where the Buddha was, desiring to find fault with him.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra thought to himself:
"These various non-Buddhist brahmins are coming toward the Buddha’s dwelling, wishing to find fault with him.
I shall now recite and contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā as I received it from the Buddha."
"These non-Buddhist practitioners and brahmins will ultimately be unable to create obstacles midway and sever the teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Having had this thought, Śakra Devendra immediately recited the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, the various non-Buddhist brahmins circumambulated the Buddha from afar and returned by the same path.
Then Śāriputra thought to himself:
"For what reason and by what cause have these various non-Buddhist brahmins circumambulated the Buddha from afar and returned by the same path?"
The Buddha, knowing the thoughts in Śāriputra’s mind, addressed Śāriputra:
“It is Śakra Devānām Indra who has been reciting and contemplating the Prajñāpāramitā.
For this reason, the various non-Buddhist brahmins have circumambulated the Buddha from afar and returned by the same path.”
Śāriputra! Among these non-Buddhist brahmins, I do not see even a single thought of goodness.
These non-Buddhist brahmins come with malicious intent, seeking to find fault with the Buddha.

Śāriputra! When the Prajñāpāramitā is being taught, I do not see anyone in all the worlds—whether among the devas, māras, or brahmās, or within the assemblies of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—who, harboring evil intent, could find any fault in it.
Why is this? Śāriputra, within this trichiliocosm,
from the gods of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas protect this Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? It is because all these devas and humans are born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!..."

In as many lands throughout the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River, all the Buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others, all protect this Prajñāpāramitā.
"Why is this? It is because all these Buddhas and others are born from the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Māra, the Evil One, thought to himself:

"Now the fourfold assembly of the Buddha is gathered here in person, as are the devaputras of the desire realm and the form realm; among them there must surely be bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have received the prediction that they shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"I shall go to where the Buddha is and destroy his resolve.
At that time, Māra the Evil One manifested fourfold armies and approached the Buddha's dwelling. Then Śakra Devānām Indra thought to himself:
"These fourfold armies must have been manifested by Māra the Evil One; he wishes to come toward the Buddha."

Why is this? This array of fourfold forces is not comparable to the fourfold forces of King Bimbisāra, nor is it comparable to the fourfold forces of King Prasenajit, nor is it comparable to the fourfold forces of the Śākyas, nor is it comparable to the fourfold forces of the Licchavis; these are the fourfold forces conjured by Māra, the Evil One.
"This evil Māra has long sought an opportunity to harm the Buddha and wishes to afflict sentient beings.
I should instead recite the Prajñāpāramitā.
Thereupon, Śakra-devānām-indra immediately recited the Prajñāpāramitā; upon hearing his recitation, the evil Māra gradually retraced his path and departed.

At that time, the sons of the gods from the Four Great Kings up to those of the Akaniṣṭha heaven within the assembly manifested celestial flowers, scattering them from the midst of the sky over the Buddha, and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
May the Prajñāpāramitā long abide in Jambudvīpa. Why is this?

Because as long as the people of Jambudvīpa uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, for that duration the Jewel of the Buddha shall also abide without perishing, and the Jewels of the Dharma and the Saṅgha shall likewise abide without perishing.
At that time, the devas in worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, also scattered flowers and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that the Prajñāpāramitā may long abide in Jambudvīpa.”
If the Prajñāpāramitā remains for a long time, as do the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, as well as this sūtra volume, then that place will be illuminated and freed from all darkness.
The Buddha told Śakra Devānām-indra and the other devaputras:
“So it is, so it is! Kauśika and you devaputras!”
When the people of Jambudvīpa receive, uphold, and dwell with the Prajñāpāramitā, wherever that sūtra volume remains, that place shall be illuminated and freed from all darkness.
At that time, the sons of the gods manifested celestial flowers and scattered them over the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If there are good men or good women who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā, Māra or the subjects of Māra will be unable to find an opportunity against them."
World-Honored One!
We, too, shall protect these good men and good women. Why is this?
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, upholds, and even correctly recollects the Prajñāpāramitā, we regard such a person as a Buddha or as one next to a Buddha.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

It should be known that those sons and daughters of good family who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā have, in previous lives, performed much meritorious work for the Buddhas, have drawn near to and made offerings to the Buddhas, and have been protected by spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).”
"Bhagavān! The omniscience of all Buddhas should be sought from within the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the perfection of wisdom should likewise be sought from within omniscience."

Why is this? The perfection of wisdom is not different from omniscience, and omniscience is not different from the perfection of wisdom; the perfection of wisdom and omniscience are non-dual and indistinguishable.
"Therefore, we regard such a person as being the Buddha himself, or next to the Buddha.
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra: "So it is, so it is!"
Kauśika! The omniscience of all Buddhas is precisely the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and the perfection of wisdom is precisely omniscience. Why is this?
Kauśika! All the omniscience of the Buddhas is born from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
The perfection of wisdom is not different from omniscience, and omniscience is not different from the perfection of wisdom; the perfection of wisdom and omniscience are non-dual and undifferentiated.

Chapter 36: The Honored Guide. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Chapter Thirty-Six, "The Honored Guide" (in the old translation, "Ānanda’s Praise"). At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Why do you not praise the dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā, kṣāntipāramitā, vīryapāramitā, dhyānapāramitā, and even the eighteen unique qualities (āveṇikadharma), but praise only the prajñāpāramitā?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“The Prajñāpāramitā is the honored guide for the five pāramitās, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha. Ānanda!”
"What do you think? Can a gift that is not dedicated toward omniscience (sarvajñatā) be called the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā)?
"No, World-Honored One."
“Is the morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom that are not dedicated to omniscience (sarvajñā) the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
"No, World-Honored One!
For this reason, it is known that the Prajñāpāramitā is the honored guide among the five pāramitās and even up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; therefore, it is praised."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does one dedicate the gift toward omniscience (sarvajñatā) so that it becomes the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and so on, up to becoming the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“To give with the dharma of non-duality and dedicate it to sarvajñā (all-knowledge) is called dānapāramitā.
To give by dedicating it to sarvajñā through the non-arising and unobtainability [of things] is called dānapāramitā.”
Even unto the dedication of the wisdom of non-dual dharmas toward omniscience (sarvajñā), this is called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Because that which is unarisen is unattainable, the dedication of the wisdom toward omniscience is called the perfection of wisdom.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that dedicating a gift toward omniscience (sarvajñā) by means of the non-dual dharma is called the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā)?”
“...up to the point that dedicating by means of the non-dual dharma to the wisdom of *sarvajñā* is called the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“Because form is the non-dual dharma; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are the non-dual dharma; up to and including because *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is the non-dual dharma.”
“World-Honored One!
How is it that form is the non-dual dharma, and so on, up to unexcelled perfect enlightenment being the non-dual dharma?
The Buddha said:
“Form is empty of the characteristic of form. Why is this?

The perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) and form are non-dual and not distinct; even up to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttarasamyaksambodhi*) and the perfection of giving, they are non-dual and not distinct.”
The five perfections are also like this. For this reason, Ānanda,
one should praise only the Prajñāpāramitā.
It serves as the honored guide for the five perfections up to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Ānanda!
It is like the great earth: when seeds are sown within it, they arise once the conditions and causes have come together.
Just as these various seeds depend upon the earth to grow,

so too, Ānanda, the five perfections depend upon the perfection of wisdom to arise; even the four foundations of mindfulness up to the knowledge of all modes likewise depend upon the perfection of wisdom to arise.
"For this reason, Ānanda,
the perfection of wisdom is the honored guide for the five perfections, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Blessed One has said that for good men and good women who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā, their merit is inexhaustible.”
Why is this? Because by upholding the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintaining right mindfulness of it, one receives the unsurpassed path of all Buddhas of the three periods of time. Why is that?
If one wishes to attain sarvajñā (all-knowledge), one should seek it from within the prajñāpāramitā; if one wishes to attain the prajñāpāramitā, one should seek it from within sarvajñā.
World-Honored One!

Because of upholding, reciting, and correctly recollecting the Prajñāpāramitā, the ten paths of wholesome action appear in the world; the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and even the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha appear in the world.

Because they uphold the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintain right mindfulness of it, there come to be in the world the great clans of Kṣatriyas, the great clans of Brāhmaṇas, and the great households of householders, as well as the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
Because they uphold the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintain right mindfulness of it, there come to be those from the stage of Srotāpanna up to Arhat, Pratyekabuddha, and Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
"Because they uphold the Prajñāpāramitā and even maintain right mindfulness of it, the Buddhas appear in the world.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: "Kauśika!"
Noble sons and noble daughters who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā—I do not say that their merit is limited to only that much.
Why is this? Kausika!

Because these sons of good family and daughters of good family who uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, and so forth, up to correctly recollecting it without departing from the mind of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), achieve an immeasurable mass of morality, and they achieve the masses of concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Furthermore, Kauśika,

if these sons or daughters of good family are able to receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā, and do not depart from the mind of sarvajñatā (omniscience), you should know that such persons are as if they were the Buddha.
Furthermore, Kauśika!

All the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not equal the aggregates of morality up to the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of these sons and daughters of good family—not even by a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousand-millionth part, nor can they be reached by any calculation or analogy.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family have attained liberation within the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and no longer seek the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Furthermore, Kauśika!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who write out, uphold, and make offerings to a volume of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra—honoring, revering, and respecting it with flowers, incense, necklaces, and even musical performances—they too shall obtain merit in both this life and future lives.
At that time, Śakra Devānām-indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If these sons and daughters of good family receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the *prajñāpāramitā*, remaining inseparable from the mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and make offerings to the *prajñāpāramitā* with flowers, incense, and even music, honoring, respecting, and revering it;”
"I shall always protect such a person.
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra: "Kauśika!"
When these good sons and good daughters wish to read, recite, and expound this Prajñāpāramitā, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas will all come to listen to the Dharma.
When these good sons and good daughters preach the Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, the sons of the gods augment their courage and strength.
If these Dharma masters become utterly exhausted and do not wish to preach the Dharma, because the sons of the gods augment their courage and strength, they are able to preach it once again.

Good sons and good daughters who receive this Prajñāpāramitā and even maintain right mindfulness of it, and who offer it flowers, incense, and even music, shall likewise attain these merits in the present life.
Furthermore, Kauśika, when these sons and daughters of good family preach the Prajñāpāramitā among the fourfold assembly, their minds are free from timidity;
even if there are challenges or debates, they harbor no sense of fear.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family are sustained by the protection of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

Within the *prajñāpāramitā*, all phenomena are also analyzed—whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, wholesome or unwholesome, conditioned or unconditioned, the teachings of the śrāvakas, the teachings of the pratyekabuddhas, the teachings of the bodhisattvas, or the teachings of the Buddhas.

Because good sons and good daughters dwell in inner emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and existence, they do not perceive anyone who can challenge the *prajñāpāramitā*, nor do they perceive anyone who receives such a challenge, nor do they perceive the *prajñāpāramitā* itself.
In this way, because these sons and daughters of good family are protected by the *prajñāpāramitā*, no one is able to challenge or destroy them.
Furthermore, when these sons and daughters of good family receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the *prajñāpāramitā*, they do not sink, nor do they feel fear or terror.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family do not perceive any dharma that perishes or causes fear. Kausika!

Good sons and good daughters who receive, uphold, and even correctly recollect the Prajñāpāramitā, and who offer flowers, incense, and even banners and canopies, shall likewise obtain these merits in the present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, and correctly recollects the Prajñāpāramitā, and even copies and maintains its scrolls, making offerings of flowers, incense, and so forth, up to banners and canopies—such a person will be beloved by their parents, remembered by their kinsmen and friends, respected by all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, and cherished and honored by the Buddhas of the ten directions, as well as by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, pratyekabuddhas, arhats, and even srotāpannas; they will likewise be cherished and honored by all the world, whether devas, māras, brahmās, or asuras."
This person practices the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), and there is no time when this perfection of giving is interrupted.

Likewise, for the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*), and the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), there is also no time when they are interrupted.

They cultivate the emptiness of the internal without interruption, up to and including the emptiness of non-existence and existence without interruption; they cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness without interruption, up to and including the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without interruption; they cultivate the various gates of samādhi without interruption, the various gates of dhāraṇī without interruption, and the various supernormal powers of a bodhisattva without interruption; they accomplish the maturation of sentient beings and purify buddha-fields without interruption, up to and including the cultivation of the knowledge of all modes without interruption.
Such a person is also able to subdue difficult arguments and slanders.

Good sons and good daughters who receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including maintaining right mindfulness and never departing from the mind of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), and who copy and uphold the sūtra scrolls, making offerings of incense, flowers, banners, and canopies, shall likewise attain these merits in both this life and future lives.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

Wherever a son or daughter of good family writes down and maintains this sūtra volume, all the Cāturmahārājakāyika devas within that trichiliocosm who have set their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi will come to that place to behold the Prajñāpāramitā, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and pay homage to it, before returning home."

The gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmakāyika-sabhā Heaven, and the Mahābrahmā Heaven; the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, and the Ābhāsvara Heaven; the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, and the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven; the Anabhraka Heaven, the Puṇyaprasava Heaven, and the Bṛhatphala Heaven—all those who have resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* come to this place to behold the Prajñāpāramitā, receive, read, recite, and explain it, and having made offerings and prostrations, they return.

The gods of the Pure Abodes—namely, the Akaniṣṭha gods, the Sudarśana gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Atapa gods, and the Avṛha gods—all came to this place to behold this Prajñāpāramitā; they received, read, recited, and explained it, made offerings and prostrations to it, and then departed.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

The various devas from the Cāturmahārājika heaven up to the Bṛhatphala heaven throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, as well as the Śuddhāvāsa devas and other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, also come to behold the Prajñāpāramitā, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and pay homage to it, before returning."
These sons and daughters of good family should form this thought:

"The various devas of the Four Great Kings up to the Bṛhatphala devas in the worlds of the ten directions who have resolved upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, as well as the Śuddhāvāsa devas and all other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, come to behold the Prajñāpāramitā, to receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and pay homage to it."
"I have thus performed the gift of Dharma. Kausika!

All the Cāturmahārājika devas up to the Akaniṣṭha devas within this trichiliocosm, as well as all the Cāturmahārājika devas up to the Akaniṣṭha devas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have resolved their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, shall protect these good men and good women; no evils shall find an opportunity against them, except for the heavy karmic offenses of their past lives.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family shall also obtain these merits in this present life.
That is to say, all the devaputras who have resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi will all come to this place.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because these sons of the gods have resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to rescue and protect all sentient beings, not to abandon any sentient being, and to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How should good sons and good daughters know that the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven have come, as well as the gods from the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven from the lands of the ten directions, to see, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and pay homage to the Prajñāpāramitā?”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra: “Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family sees this great, pure radiance, they should know for certain that great and virtuous devas have come to see, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and prostrate before the Prajñāpāramitā.”
Furthermore, Kauśika,

if a son of good family or a daughter of good family perceives a rare and exquisite fragrance, they should know for certain that great virtuous devas have come to see, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, and prostrate before the Prajñāpāramitā at that time.
Furthermore, Kauśika,
because good sons and good daughters practice purity, the devas come to their place, behold the Prajñāpāramitā, receive, read, recite, explain, make offerings to, rejoice in, and prostrate before it.
Thereupon, the minor spirits within departed immediately, unable to endure the majestic power and virtue of these great and virtuous devas,
because those great and virtuous devas had arrived.

These good sons and good daughters have generated the great resolve; for this reason, at the place where the Prajñāpāramitā resides, there should be no impurities in the four directions. One should instead burn lamps and incense, scatter various famous flowers, smear the ground with various perfumes, and adorn it with various canopies, banners, and streamers.
Furthermore, Kauśika, when good men and good women preach the Dharma, they never experience exhaustion; they perceive their own bodies as light and their minds as joyful.
They rest in accordance with the Dharma, and whether lying down or waking, they are peaceful and secure, free from all evil dreams.

In a dream, one sees various Buddhas endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics, surrounded by a community of bhikṣus who pay them respectful homage as they preach the Dharma.

Standing beside these Buddhas, one listens to and receives their teachings—namely, the six pāramitās, the four foundations of mindfulness, and so forth, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

He discerns the meaning of the six *pāramitās*, discerns the four foundations of mindfulness, and likewise discerns the meaning of everything up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*).

He also beholds the exquisite adornments of the Bodhi tree; he sees the various bodhisattvas approaching the Bodhi tree and attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; he sees the Buddhas, having completed their enlightenment, turning the wheel of Dharma; and he sees hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas gathered together for a Dharma discourse, saying:
"One should seek *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) in this manner."
One should bring sentient beings to maturity in this way;
one should purify the Buddha-lands in this way.

Furthermore, one sees countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas in the ten directions, and hears their names—such as such-and-such a Buddha in such-and-such a direction and such-and-such a land—preaching the Dharma while surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and hundreds of thousands of millions of Śrāvakas who pay them respectful homage.
Furthermore, they see countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas throughout the ten directions entering parinirvāṇa.
They also see countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of such auspicious dreams; lying down in peace and awakening in peace.

The devas augment his vital energy, so that he becomes conscious of his body being light and agile; he no longer feels great craving for food, drink, clothing, bedding, or medicinal decoctions, and his mind remains detached toward these four types of offerings.

For example, it is like a bhikṣu practicing dhyāna; having arisen from meditative concentration, his mind remains in union with that concentration, and he does not crave food or drink, for his mind is light and subtle. Why is this?
Kauśika! It is the natural law for the gods that they should strengthen their vital energy with the essence of various flavors;
likewise, the Buddhas of the ten directions, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, also strengthen their vital energy.

Thus it is, Kauśika! A son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to obtain such merit in this present life should accept, uphold, draw near to, read, recite, explain, and correctly contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā, and should likewise never be separated from the mind of omniscience (sarvajñatā-citta).

Kauśika! Although good sons and good daughters may not be able to receive, uphold, or even correctly recollect [this teaching], they should nevertheless transcribe and preserve the sūtra scrolls, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising them with incense, flowers, necklaces, and even banners and canopies.

Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family hears this Prajñāpāramitā, receives, upholds, recites, explains, and correctly contemplates it; and if they copy it into a volume, honoring, making offerings to, respecting, and praising it with flowers, incense, and even banners and canopies.
The merit of these sons and daughters of good family is exceedingly great.

It surpasses that of one who makes offerings to the Buddhas and their disciples throughout the ten directions— revering, honoring, and praising them with robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicinal elixirs— and further surpasses that of one who,

after the parinirvāṇa of those Buddhas and their disciples, erects stūpas of the seven precious substances and reverently makes offerings, honors, and praises them with flowers, incense, and even banners and canopies.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Nine; The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Ten.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of Kucha during the Later Qin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-Seven: On Dharmodgata.
The Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
If one portion were made of the Buddha’s relics filling the entire Jambudvīpa, and another portion were a written scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
between these two portions, which would you take?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Suppose there were one portion consisting of the Buddha’s relics filling the entirety of Jambudvīpa, and another portion consisting of a single scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.”
Of these two portions, I would rather take this scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra. Why is that,
World-Honored One?
It is not that I lack reverence for the Buddha’s relics, nor do I fail to honor them,
World-Honored One.
It is because these relics are born from the *prajñāpāramitā* and have been cultivated and perfumed by the *prajñāpāramitā* that they receive offerings, reverence, respect, and praise.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Śakra Devānām Indra:
"Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā cannot be grasped; it is without color, without form, and without resistance; it has a single characteristic, which is the so-called 'characteristicless'."
How could you wish to grasp it? Why is this?

This Prajñāpāramitā does not arise for the sake of grasping, nor does it arise for the sake of relinquishing; it does not arise for the sake of increase or decrease, accumulation or dispersal, loss or gain, defilement or purity.
This Prajñāpāramitā does not bestow the dharmas of the Buddhas, nor does it abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons;
it does not bestow the dharmas of Pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of Arhats, or the dharmas of those in training, nor does it abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons;
it does not bestow the unconditioned nature, nor does it abandon the conditioned nature.

He does not associate with inner emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence, nor with the four foundations of mindfulness up to all-knowledge, yet he does not abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said to Śāriputra: “So it is, so it is! Śāriputra!”

If there is anyone who knows this Prajñāpāramitā, they neither associate with the dharmas of the Buddhas nor abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons; even so, they neither associate with the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā) nor abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to practice the perfection of wisdom and is able to cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
Why is this? Because the perfection of wisdom does not operate with respect to the characteristics of dualistic phenomena.
“The characteristic of non-duality is the perfection of wisdom; the characteristic of non-duality is the perfection of meditation, and so on, up to the perfection of generosity.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
Kauśika! It is as you have said:
because the prajñāpāramitā does not operate within the characteristics of dualistic dharmas.
