"What the World-Honored One has spoken is inconceivable.
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Because form (*rūpa*) is inconceivable, what is spoken is inconceivable; because feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*) are inconceivable, what is spoken is inconceivable; because the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*) are inconceivable, what is spoken is inconceivable; and so on, up to because all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) is inconceivable, what is spoken is inconceivable."

Subhūti! When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they know that form is inconceivable; they know that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable; and so on, up to knowing that all-knowledge is inconceivable.
"Such a bodhisattva would then be unable to fulfill the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who will be able to believe and understand this profound *prajñāpāramitā*?
The Buddha said,

"If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have long practiced the six *pāramitās*, planted roots of goodness, extensively attended upon and made offerings to the Buddhas, and associated with spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), these bodhisattvas will be able to believe and understand the profound *prajñāpāramitā*."
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One,

how is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the six pāramitās, planted roots of goodness, extensively attended upon and made offerings to the Buddhas, and associated with virtuous friends?”
The Buddha said:
“If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not discriminate form, does not discriminate the characteristics of form, and does not discriminate the nature of form;
and does not discriminate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor discriminate the characteristics of consciousness, nor discriminate the nature of consciousness.”
It is likewise for the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; for forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects; and from the eye-element up to the consciousness-element.
One does not discriminate between the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm, nor does one discriminate the characteristics or natures of these three realms.

One does not discriminate between the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) and so forth up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*); nor between internal emptiness (*adhyātmaśūnyatā*) and so forth up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence (*abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā*); nor between the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) and so forth up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*); nor between the ten powers of a Buddha (*buddhabala*) and so forth up to the eighteen unique qualities (*āveṇikadharma*). One does not discriminate between giving and so forth up to the eighteen unique wisdoms; one does not discriminate the characteristics of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*); and one does not discriminate the nature of the knowledge of all modes.
Why is this? Subhūti! Form is inconceivable;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable; even up to all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), it is inconceivable.

Thus it is, Subhūti! This is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has long practiced the six pāramitās, planted roots of goodness, extensively attended upon and made offerings to the Buddhas, and associated with virtuous spiritual friends.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Because form is profound, the Prajñāpāramitā is profound; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound, and so on up to the knowledge of all modes, the Prajñāpāramitā is profound.”
World-Honored One!

This Prajñāpāramitā is a treasury of jewels, because it contains the jewel of the fruit of srotāpanna; because it contains the jewels of the fruits of sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, arhat, the path of the pratyekabuddha, and anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Because they are the jewels of the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers; of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; of the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered knowledges, great loving-kindness and great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities; and of omniscience and the knowledge of all modes.
World-Honored One!
This perfection of wisdom is a pure accumulation.
Because form is pure, the perfection of wisdom is a pure accumulation.
“Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are pure, up to and including the purity of all-knowledge, the perfection of wisdom is a mass of purity. Subhūti said:
“World-Honored One!”
"It is truly strange that when this Prajñāpāramitā is being taught, there are so many obstacles.
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is!"
Subhūti! This profound Prajñāpāramitā will encounter many obstacles.
For this reason, when a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to write down this Prajñāpāramitā, they should write it down with haste.
When one is reading, reciting, contemplating, explaining, correctly recollecting, and practicing [this], one should also practice with urgency. Why is this?

It is because when one is writing, reading, reciting, contemplating, explaining, correctly recollecting, and practicing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one does not wish for various obstacles to arise.
Good sons and good daughters, if you can complete the transcription in one month, you should transcribe it with diligence.
Whether it takes two months, three months, four months, five months, six months, seven months, or even a year to complete the transcription, you should likewise transcribe it with diligence.

Through reciting, contemplating, explaining, correctly recollecting, and practicing, whether one attains accomplishment in one month or even in one year, one should diligently strive for accomplishment.
Why is this? Subhūti,
it is because many difficulties arise regarding these precious treasures.
Subhūti said: “World-Honored One!

Because Māra, the Evil One, delights in creating obstacles within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he prevents it from being written down, and prevents it from being read, recited, contemplated, explained, correctly recollected, and practiced.”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Although evil Māra may wish to create obstacles for this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, preventing its being written down, read, recited, contemplated, explained, correctly recollected, or practiced, he will nonetheless be unable to destroy this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s writing of the *prajñāpāramitā* up to its practice.”
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
By whose power is it that the evil Māra is unable to obstruct or hinder a bodhisattva mahāsattva from copying the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to and including its practice?”
The Buddha said:
"It is by the power of the Buddha that Māra, the Evil One, is unable to obstruct or hinder a bodhisattva mahāsattva in writing, reciting, or even practicing the profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Śāriputra! It is also by the power of the Buddhas currently residing in the lands of the ten directions, and because those Buddhas protect and keep this bodhisattva in mind, that Māra is unable to obstruct or hinder the bodhisattva-mahāsattva from copying, accomplishing, or even practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*.

Why is this? Because throughout the lands of the ten directions, the present immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas protect and keep in mind this Bodhisattva who writes out the profound Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including its practice; such is the natural law, and none shall be able to create obstacles.
Śāriputra! Good sons and good daughters should form this thought:
"That I write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā and even practice it is entirely through the power of the Buddhas of the ten directions."
Śāriputra said: “World-Honored One!

If there are good sons or good daughters who write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā and even practice it, all of this is due to the power of the Buddha; one should know that such persons are protected by all the Buddhas.”
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is! Śāriputra!"

It should be known that if any son of good family or daughter of good family writes down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and even practices it, it is all due to the power of the Buddhas; it should be known that they are likewise protected by all the Buddhas.
Śāriputra said: “World-Honored One!

The immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions all know, and all see with their Buddha-eye, these good sons and good daughters while they are writing the profound Prajñāpāramitā, and even while they are practicing it.”
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is! Śāriputra!"

The present Buddhas of the ten directions, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable in number, all know and all behold with their Buddha-eyes these good men and good women while they are writing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and even while they are practicing it.
Śāriputra! Among these,

if a son of good family or a daughter of good family seeking the bodhisattva path writes down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, upholds, reads, recites, correctly contemplates, and practices it according to the teaching, you should know that such a person is close to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* before long.

Śāriputra! If good sons and good daughters write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive, uphold, read, recite, and even correctly contemplate it; if these persons possess faith and understanding in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and furthermore offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, making offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, and even banners and canopies—[they shall obtain great merit].
Śāriputra! All Buddhas recognize these good men and good women, and all see them with their Buddha-eye.
The merit of these good men and good women who make such offerings shall bring great benefit and a great karmic reward.

Śāriputra! By virtue of these causes and conditions of making such offerings, these sons and daughters of good family shall never fall into the evil realms; until they reach the stage of non-retrogression (avaivartika), they shall never be separated from the Buddhas.

Śāriputra! Because of these roots of goodness, these sons and daughters of good family will, until they reach *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, never be separated from the six *pāramitās*; they will never be separated from inner emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*); they will never be separated from the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) up to the eightfold noble path; and they will never be separated from the ten powers of a Buddha (*buddha-bala*) up to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra! This profound *prajñāpāramitā* shall, after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, reach the lands of the south.
Therein, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen shall write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and they shall receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, explain, correctly recollect, and practice it.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, they shall never fall into the evil realms, but will instead experience the pleasures of gods and humans, increase the six pāramitās, and make offerings to, revere, honor, and praise all Buddhas; gradually, through the vehicles of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and Buddha, they shall attain nirvāṇa.

Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā shall proceed from the south to the west. In whatever place it resides, there the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās shall write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and they shall receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, explain, correctly attend to, and practice it.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, they shall never fall into the evil realms, but will instead experience the joys of gods and humans, further increase the six pāramitās, and make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise all Buddhas; gradually, through the vehicles of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and Buddha, they shall attain nirvāṇa.

Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā shall proceed from the western direction to the northern direction. In whatever place it resides, there the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās shall write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and they shall receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, explain, correctly attend to, and practice it.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, they shall never fall into the evil realms, but will instead experience the pleasures of gods and humans, increase the six pāramitās, and offer worship, respect, reverence, and praise to all Buddhas; gradually, through the vehicles of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and Buddha, they shall attain nirvāṇa.
Śāriputra! At that time, this profound Prajñāpāramitā shall perform the work of a Buddha in the northern direction. Why is this?
Śāriputra, when my Dharma flourishes, it possesses no characteristic of extinction. Śāriputra!
I have already kept in mind these good men and good women who receive this profound Prajñāpāramitā and even practice it;
these good men and good women are able to transcribe this Prajñāpāramitā and reverently offer it, honoring, respecting, and praising it with flowers, incense, and even banners and canopies.

Śāriputra! Because of these roots of goodness as causes and conditions, these sons and daughters of good family shall never fall into the evil realms, but will instead experience the pleasures of devas and humans, increase the six pāramitās, and make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise all Buddhas; they will gradually attain nirvāṇa by means of the vehicles of the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and Buddha.
Why is this? Śāriputra! With my Buddha-eye I see such persons, and I likewise praise and extol them.
"In the lands of the ten directions, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas likewise see this person with their Buddha-eye, and they also praise and extol them.
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Will this profound Prajñāpāramitā later be widely practiced in the northern region?
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is!"
Śāriputra! This profound Prajñāpāramitā shall later be widely practiced in the northern region. Śāriputra!

In the future, in the northern region, if these sons or daughters of good family hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, or if they write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, contemplate and explain it, correctly bring it to mind, and practice according to its teaching, you should know that these sons and daughters of good family have long since set their minds upon the Mahāyāna, have made offerings to many Buddhas, have planted roots of goodness, and have long associated with virtuous friends.
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In the future, how many sons of good family and daughters of good family will there be in the northern direction who seek the path of the Buddha, who will copy the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and even practice it according to the teaching?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"In the future, although there will be many sons and daughters of good family in the northern direction who seek the path of the Buddha, few will hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and remain undaunted, unstartled, unafraid, and without fear."

Why is this? Because such a person has extensively approached and made offerings to the Buddhas, and has extensively questioned the Buddhas; such a person will certainly be able to fulfill the perfection of wisdom (prajñā-pāramitā), the perfection of meditation (dhyāna-pāramitā), the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā), the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā), the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā), and the perfection of generosity (dāna-pāramitā); they will fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni) up to and including the fulfillment of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇika-buddhadharma).
Śāriputra! Because the roots of goodness of these sons and daughters of good family have fully matured, they are able to greatly benefit sentient beings for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Why is this? It is because I now teach the Dharma corresponding to *sarvajñatā* for these sons and daughters of good family; likewise, the Buddhas of the past also taught the Dharma corresponding to *sarvajñatā* for these sons and daughters of good family.

By reason of these causes and conditions, when this person is born in future lives, they will continue to attain the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and will also explain the dharma of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi to others.

These sons and daughters of good family are all united in single-minded harmony; neither Māra nor his followers can thwart their resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, let alone those who practice evil or disparage those who practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* being able to destroy their resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family who seek the bodhisattva path, upon hearing this profound Prajñāpāramitā, attain great joy and delight in the Dharma, and they also establish many others in roots of goodness for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
These sons and daughters of good family have made a vow before me:

"When I practice the bodhisattva path, I shall deliver countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them, until they reach the stage of non-retrogression and receive their prediction."
I know their minds, and I likewise rejoice in them.
These sons and daughters of good family have also made a vow before the Buddhas of the past:

"When I practice the bodhisattva path, I shall deliver countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them, until they reach the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*) and receive their prediction."
"The Buddhas of the past also knew their minds and rejoiced in them. Śāriputra!

These sons and daughters of good family possess great resolve; the forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and dharmas they receive are also great, and they are likewise able to practice great giving."
Having been able to perform great giving, one plants great roots of goodness.
Having planted great roots of goodness, one attains great retribution.
For the sake of gathering in sentient beings, one takes on a body and is able to relinquish all internal and external possessions among those beings.
By means of these roots of goodness, they make a vow to be born in other lands where the present Buddhas are currently expounding the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā* before those Buddhas, they likewise instruct, exhort, benefit, and gladden hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings there, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra said to the Buddha, “It is rare, World-Honored One!

Regarding the dharmas of the past, future, and present, there is no dharma that the Buddha does not know, and no suchness of dharmas that he does not know; there is no aspect of the conduct of sentient beings that he does not know.”

Now the Buddha fully knows all past Buddhas, as well as their bodhisattvas and śrāvakas; he also knows all present Buddhas throughout the ten directions, as well as the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas in their buddha-fields; and he likewise knows all future Buddhas, as well as their bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
“World-Honored One!

In future ages, there will be good men and good women who diligently seek the six pāramitās, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, and even practicing them; some will attain them, while others will not.”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“If good sons and good daughters seek with single-minded diligence and vigor, they shall obtain the various sūtras corresponding to the six pāramitās.”
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If good men and good women practice with such diligence, will they obtain these profound sūtras that correspond to the six pāramitās?”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“These sons and daughters of good family shall obtain these profound sūtras corresponding to the six pāramitās. Why is this?

Good sons and good daughters, for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they preach the Dharma to sentient beings, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening them, so as to cause them to abide in the six pāramitās.
For this reason, after this life, these sons and daughters of good family will be reborn in future lives where they easily obtain profound sutras corresponding to the six pāramitās.

Having obtained them, they will practice with diligent effort as taught in the six pāramitās without ceasing, until they purify buddha-fields, bring sentient beings to maturity, and attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Chapter 46: On the Deeds of Māra. The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Forty-six: On the Deeds of Māra. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
These good sons and good daughters have resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, practicing the six *pāramitās* to bring sentient beings to maturity and purify Buddha-fields.
The Buddha has already praised and described their merits.
World-Honored One,
how is it that these good men and good women who seek the Buddha-way encounter various obstacles?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If eloquence for joyful exposition does not arise immediately, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva. Subhūti said:
“World-Honored One!
For what reason and by what causes and conditions does the eloquence of joyful exposition fail to arise immediately? This is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
The Buddha said:
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, it is difficult to fully complete the six perfections.
Because of these causes and conditions, if eloquence for joyful exposition does not immediately arise, this is a work of Māra for that bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If eloquence for preaching suddenly arises, you should know that this too is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason is it that the sudden arising of eloquence in joyful preaching is also a work of Māra?
The Buddha said,
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the dāna-pāramitā up to the prajñā-pāramitā, they become attached to the joy of preaching the Dharma."
For these reasons, if eloquence for preaching arises suddenly, one should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, when copying this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, if one is haughty and arrogant, one should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti! When copying this sutra, if one is distracted by laughter and jesting, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Furthermore, Subhūti!
If, while copying this sutra, one laughs lightly and shows disrespect, you should know that this is the work of Māra toward a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, if, while copying this sutra,
the mind is distracted and unsettled, you should know that this is the work of Māra toward a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti! When this sutra is being transcribed, if there is mutual discord among the participants, you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a son or daughter of good family thinks,
"I do not find any flavor in this sutra," and then abandons it and departs,
you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when one receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, or correctly contemplates the Prajñāpāramitā, if one becomes haughty and arrogant, you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when one is upholding the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, or when one is drawing near to it and correctly recollecting it, if they mock and ridicule one another, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, Subhūti, when one upholds the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
recites it, correctly contemplates it, and practices it, if they treat one another with contempt, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
If, while upholding, reciting, or even correctly reflecting upon the Prajñāpāramitā, one’s mind becomes distracted, you should know that this is an act of Māra for a bodhisattva.
If, while upholding, reciting, or even correctly contemplating the Prajñāpāramitā, the mind is not in harmony, one should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One! The World-Honored One has said:”
“Good sons and good daughters may think:
‘I do not find the flavor within these sutras,’ and they then abandon them and depart; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.”
“World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition does a bodhisattva fail to find the flavor within the sūtras and then abandon them?
The Buddha said:

"This bodhisattva mahāsattva did not practice the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, or the perfection of generosity for long in previous lives."
When this person hears this teaching on the Prajñāpāramitā, they rises from their seat and thinks to themselves:
"I am not recorded within the Prajñāpāramitā."
"With a mind that is not pure, he then rises from his seat and departs; you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what reason do they not receive a prediction [of enlightenment], but rather rise from their seats and depart when this Prajñāpāramitā is being taught?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"If a bodhisattva has not yet entered the fixed position of the Dharma (dharmatāniyāma), the Buddhas do not grant them the prediction of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Furthermore, Subhūti, when the Prajñāpāramitā is being taught, a bodhisattva forms this thought:
"I have no name therein."
"If their mind is not pure, you should know that this is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Subhūti asked:
"For what reason is the name of this bodhisattva not mentioned within this profound Prajñāpāramitā?"
The Buddha said:
“For bodhisattvas who have not yet received a prediction, the Buddhas do not record their names.
Furthermore, Subhūti!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"Within this prajñāpāramitā, there is no place of birth, no name, nor any village, town, or city for me."

If such a person does not wish to hear the Prajñāpāramitā and departs from the assembly, at the very moment they conceive that thought, for every single thought-moment they have retreated by one kalpa; they must instead strive with even greater diligence and vigor to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva studies other sūtras while abandoning the *prajñāpāramitā*, they will ultimately be unable to reach omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
One should know that for a son or daughter of good family to abandon the root and grasp at branches and leaves is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What are those other sūtras that, when studied by good sons and good daughters, do not lead them to sarvajñā (all-knowledge)?”
The Buddha said:

“These are the sūtras that śrāvakas should practice, namely: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the eightfold noble path, and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.”

When good sons or good daughters abide in this, they attain the fruit of srotāpanna, the fruit of sakṛdāgāmin, the fruit of anāgāmin, and the fruit of arhat; this is called the practice of the śrāvakas, and it cannot reach sarvajñatā.
In this way, sons or daughters of good family abandon the *prajñāpāramitā* and draw near to these other sutras.
Why is that? Subhūti!
From within the Prajñāpāramitā, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are born, and they accomplish both mundane and supramundane dharmas. Subhūti,
when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas study the Prajñāpāramitā, they also study mundane and supramundane dharmas.
Subhūti! It is as if a dog, instead of seeking food from its master, were to beg from the laborers. Thus it is, Subhūti!

In future ages, if there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to grasp at branches and leaves, taking up those sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, you should know that this is a demonic deed (*mārakarman*) for bodhisattvas.
Subhūti! It is as if, for example, there were a person who wished to see an elephant, yet having seen it, instead went back to examine its footprints. Subhūti!
"What do you think? Is this person wise? Subhūti replied, "He is not wise."
The Buddha said:
"It is the same for all sons and daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha.
Having obtained the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they abandon it and instead take up the sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
Subhūti! You should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Subhūti!
It is like a person who wishes to see the great ocean, yet instead seeks water in a cow’s footprint, thinking:
"Can the water of the great ocean be equal to this?"
“Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
“It is not wise,” the Buddha said.

“In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha and act in this same way: having obtained the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they abandon it and instead take up the sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. You should know that this, too, is a work of Māra for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
Subhūti! It is as if a master carpenter, or a carpenter’s apprentice, were to intend to construct the Victorious Palace of Śakra while taking the palaces of the sun and moon as their model.
"Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"It is not wise. "It is so, Subhūti!

In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family with meager merit who seek the Buddha-way; having obtained this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will abandon it and instead seek *sarvajñatā* within the sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
“Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"It is not wise. The Buddha said,
"You should know that this, too, is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
Subhūti! It is as if there were a person who wished to see a universal monarch (cakravartin), but having seen him, did not recognize him.
Later, seeing various minor kings, he took their physical characteristics and spoke thus:
"How does this differ from a Wheel-Turning Sage King?
"Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise?"
Subhūti said: "It is not wise. [The Buddha said: "Subhūti!"

In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family with meager merit who seek the Buddha-way; having obtained this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they will abandon it and instead take up and uphold the sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in their quest for sarvajñatā.
"Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"It is not wise. "Subhūti,
you should know that this is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva."
“Suppose, for example, a hungry person were to obtain food of a hundred flavors, yet discard it and instead eat sixty-day-old grain porridge.
Subhūti, what do you think? Would this person be wise?”
Subhūti said: "It is not wise. The Buddha said:

"In a future age, there will be sons and daughters of good family who seek the Buddha-way; having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will abandon it and instead take up and uphold those sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, seeking *sarvajñatā* [omniscience] thereby."
"What do you think? Is this person wise? Subhūti replied, "He is not wise."
“You should know that this, too, is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Subhūti,
it is like a person who, having obtained a priceless maṇi jewel, instead compares it to a crystal gem.”
"Subhūti, what do you think? Would such a person be considered wise? Subhūti replied:
"It is not wise," the Buddha said.

"In future ages, there will be sons and daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha; having heard this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they will abandon it and instead take up the sūtras practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, seeking sarvajñatā thereby."
"Would this person be considered clever?
Subhūti replied, "He would not be considered clever."
"You should know that this, too, is the work of Māra against a bodhisattva. Furthermore, Subhūti,

when these sons of good family or daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha are transcribing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they delight in discoursing on matters that are not in accordance with the Dharma, and thus they fail to complete the transcription of the *prajñāpāramitā*."

That is to say: delighting in speaking of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena; delighting in speaking of the precepts, meditative concentration, and the formless attainments; delighting in speaking of the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom; and delighting in speaking of the four foundations of mindfulness up to unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Subhūti, within this prajñāpāramitā there is no characteristic of delight in discourse.

Subhūti! The Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being inconceivable; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being neither born nor extinguished; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being neither defiled nor pure; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being neither agitated nor dispersed; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being ineffable; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being without words and without meaning; the Prajñāpāramitā has the characteristic of being non-apprehensible.
Why is this? Subhūti! Within the prajñāpāramitā, these various dharmas do not exist.

Subhūti! If there are good men or good women seeking the bodhisattva path who, while writing this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, do so with a distracted mind regarding these dharmas, you should know that this, too, is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
can this Prajñāpāramitā be written down?”
The Buddha said,
"It cannot be written down. Why is this?"

Because the *prajñāpāramitā* lacks intrinsic nature, the *dhyānapāramitā*, *vīryapāramitā*, *kṣāntipāramitā*, *śīlapāramitā*, *dānapāramitā*, and so forth, up to the *sarvākārajñatā*, lack intrinsic nature.
If something lacks intrinsic nature, it is not called a "dharma.
A non-dharma cannot write upon a non-dharma. Subhūti!
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family seeking the bodhisattva path should think,
"The dharma is not this profound *prajñāpāramitā*," you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.
“World-Honored One!
Those sons and daughters of good family who seek the bodhisattva path, by means of writing out the Prajñāpāramitā, think to themselves:
‘I am writing this Prajñāpāramitā.’”
"To attach words to the Prajñāpāramitā should also be known as a work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Why is this,
World-Honored One?"
This Prajñāpāramitā is without letters; likewise, the Dhyānapāramitā, Vīryapāramitā, Kṣāntipāramitā, Śīlapāramitā, and Dānapāramitā are without letters.
World-Honored One!
Form has no words; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have no words; even up to all-knowledge, they have no words.
World-Honored One!

If good sons or good daughters seeking the bodhisattva path become attached to the letterless Prajñāpāramitā, and even become attached to the letterless knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā), you should know that this too is a demonic deed of a bodhisattva.
"Reciting, explaining, correctly recollecting, and practicing according to the teaching are also like this.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, when sons or daughters of good family who seek the Buddha-way are copying this Prajñāpāramitā, thoughts of countries arise; thoughts of villages arise; thoughts of cities and fortresses arise; thoughts of directions arise. Or, upon hearing their teacher being slandered, thoughts arise; or they think of their parents, brothers, sisters, and other relatives; or they think of bandits; or they think of caṇḍālas; or they think of groups of women, or they think of prostitutes."

In this way, through various other such distractions and obstacles, Māra further encourages these thoughts to destroy the writing of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and to destroy its recitation, reading, exposition, correct mindfulness, and practice according to the teaching.
Subhūti! You should know that this, too, is the work of Māra for a bodhisattva. Furthermore, Subhūti!

Good sons and good daughters who seek the Buddha-way receive fame, honor, and offerings of sustenance—namely, clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicines for illness, and various articles of pleasure.

When a son or daughter of good family writes down this Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, and while receiving, reading, reciting, and even correctly contemplating it, becomes attached to these activities and fails to complete the writing of the Prajñāpāramitā up to its correct contemplation—one should know that this, too, is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva.

Furthermore, Subhūti, when sons and daughters of good family who seek the Buddha-way write out the *prajñāpāramitā* and even practice it as taught, an evil Māra may employ skillful means to provide them with various other profound sūtras. A bodhisattva mahāsattva who possesses the power of skillful means should not become greedily attached to those other profound sūtras given by the evil Māra.
Why is this? Because this sutra cannot cause people to reach *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).
In this regard, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who lack skillful means, upon hearing these other profound sutras, will abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Subhūti! Within this Prajñāpāramitā, I have extensively expounded the path of skillful means for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should seek it from herein.

Subhūti! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family seeking the bodhisattva path now abandons this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and seeks the way of skillful means within the profound sūtras given by Māra concerning the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, you should know that this, too, is a work of Māra for a bodhisattva.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Thirteen; The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Fourteen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of Kucha during the Later Qin dynasty.
Chapter 47: On the Two Faults (The *Dvaya-doṣa-varga* in the *Dān-luǎng-bùhé-pǐn*).
"Furthermore, Subhūti, suppose a person who hears the Dharma wishes to write down, uphold, read, recite, inquire about the meaning of, and correctly attend to the *prajñāpāramitā*."
If the teacher of the Dharma is indolent and does not wish to explain it,
you should know that this is a work of Māra for the bodhisattva. Subhūti!
If the person who preaches the Dharma is diligent and untiring, desiring that others write down and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā,
while the listener is unwilling to receive it—
if these two minds are not in harmony, one should know this to be the work of Māra.
Furthermore, Subhūti, it may be that the person who hears the Dharma wishes to write down, uphold, read, recite, and even correctly contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā,
while the person who preaches the Dharma intends to go to another region.
Subhūti, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
When a teacher of the Dharma wishes to cause others to write down and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā;
If a listener of the Dharma wishes to go to another region,
yet their two minds are not in harmony, you should know that this is the work of Māra. "Furthermore, Subhūti!
The Dharma-preacher values the offering of robes, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and other necessities of life;
the Dharma-hearer has few desires and is content, practices seclusion, and maintains mindfulness, diligence, single-mindedness, and wisdom.

When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down, uphold, receive, read, recite, inquire into the meaning of, or maintain right mindfulness of the *prajñāpāramitā*; you should know that this is the work of Māra.
Subhūti! The Dharma-preacher has few desires and is content, practices the conduct of seclusion, and possesses mindfulness, diligence, single-mindedness, and wisdom;
yet the listener values the giving of clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and other necessities of life.

When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down, uphold, read, recite, inquire into the meaning of, or maintain right mindfulness of the Prajñāpāramitā; you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the teacher of the Dharma observes the twelve dhūtas:

first, dwelling in an araṇya; second, always begging for food; third, wearing robes made of rags; fourth, eating in a single sitting; fifth, moderation in eating; sixth, not drinking liquids after midday; seventh, dwelling among graves; eighth, dwelling at the foot of a tree; ninth, dwelling in the open air; tenth, always sitting without lying down; eleventh, begging for food in successive order; and twelfth, possessing only the three robes."

If those who listen to the Dharma do not accept the twelve dhūtas, from not dwelling in an araṇya up to not accepting the practice of wearing only three robes, then because the two parties are not in harmony, they will be unable to write down, uphold, read, recite, inquire about the meaning of, or correctly bring to mind the Prajñāpāramitā; you should know that this is the work of Māra.
Subhūti! Suppose a listener of the Dharma observes the twelve dhūtas, dwells as an araṇya-dweller, and so forth, even accepting only the three robes;
yet the teacher of the Dharma does not observe the twelve dhūtas, does not dwell as an araṇya-dweller, and so forth, nor accepts only the three robes.

When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down, uphold, read, recite, inquire about the meaning of, or maintain right mindfulness of the Prajñāpāramitā; you should know that this constitutes the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, it may be that the teacher of the Dharma possesses faith and virtue, and desires to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* up to correctly recollecting it;
yet the listener of the Dharma lacks faith, violates the precepts, and engages in evil conduct, and thus does not desire to write down, receive, or correctly recollect the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
You should know that this is the work of Māra.
Subhūti! There may be a listener of the Dharma who possesses faith and maintains the precepts well; yet—
If the one who preaches the Dharma lacks faith, violates the precepts, and engages in evil conduct, these two will not be in harmony;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If the one who preaches the Dharma is able to practice total giving with a mind free from stinginess,
while the one who listens to the Dharma is miserly and does not relinquish anything,
you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Subhūti! The listener is able to give everything and has no stinginess in heart,
yet the teacher of the Dharma is parsimonious regarding the Dharma and does not bestow it."

"When there is discord between the two, and one is unable to write down, uphold, or even maintain right mindfulness of the *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The listeners wish to provide the Dharma-preacher with the requisites of life— clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and other necessities—
but the Dharma-preacher does not wish to accept them.
One should know that this is the work of Māra.
Subhūti, there may be a teacher of the Dharma who wishes to provide for the listeners with clothing and even all other necessities of life; yet—
If the listener does not wish to receive it,
and the two do not harmonize, such that they are unable to write down, uphold, or even correctly recollect the *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, it may be that the one who preaches the Dharma is easy to understand,
while the person who listens is dull-witted."
Subhūti, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
The listener of the Dharma is easily awakened; yet—

If the teacher of the Dharma is dull-witted and the two of them do not harmonize, such that they are unable to write down, uphold, or even correctly recollect the *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, there may be a teacher of the Dharma who understands the sequential meaning of the twelve divisions of the scriptures— from the *sūtras* up to the *upadeśas*—
while the listener of the Dharma does not understand the sequential meaning of the twelve divisions of the scriptures."
One should know that this is the work of Māra:
the listener understands the sequential meaning of the twelve divisions of the scriptures,
while the speaker does not understand the sequential meaning of the twelve divisions of the scriptures.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti..."
If the teacher of the Dharma has accomplished the six pāramitās,
but the listener of the Dharma has not accomplished the six pāramitās,
and the two are thus not in harmony, they will be unable to write out the profound Prajñāpāramitā, nor even to maintain right mindfulness of it; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
If the listener possesses the six pāramitās while the teacher lacks the six pāramitās, these two will not be in harmony;
they will be unable to write down the profound Prajñāpāramitā or even maintain right mindfulness of it. One should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, it may be that the teacher of the Dharma possesses skillful means regarding the six pāramitās,
while the listener of the Dharma lacks skillful means regarding the six pāramitās."
When these two do not harmonize, such that they are unable to write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness, you should know this to be the work of Māra.
It may be that the listener possesses skillful means regarding the six *pāramitās*,
while the teacher lacks skillful means regarding the six *pāramitās*.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If the teacher of the Dharma has attained dhāraṇī, but the listener lacks dhāraṇī, these two will not be in harmony.
They will be unable to write down the profound Prajñāpāramitā, nor even maintain right mindfulness of it; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
If the listener attains dhāraṇī while the speaker lacks dhāraṇī, these two will not be in harmony;
they will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor even maintain right mindfulness of it. You should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, it may be that the teacher of the Dharma wishes for others to write down, uphold, read, recite, and even correctly contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā;
yet the listener of the Dharma does not wish to write down, uphold, read, recite, or even correctly contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā."
When the two do not harmonize, such that they are unable to write down the *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness,
one should know that this is the work of Māra. It may be that the listener wishes to write, read, recite, and explain the *prajñāpāramitā*,
while the speaker does not wish for it to be written, nor even wishes for it to be explained.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The speaker of the Dharma is free from sensual desire, ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt;
the listener of the Dharma possesses sensual desire, ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
Know that this is the work of Māra:
the listener is free from sensual desire, ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt,
while the speaker of the Dharma is possessed by sensual desire, ill will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
While one is writing out this profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even while correctly recollecting it, someone may come and speak of the intense suffering within the three evil realms, saying:
"Why do you not exhaust all suffering in this very body and quickly enter *nirvāṇa*; what use have you for this *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
"When these two do not harmonize, one will be unable to write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor even maintain right mindfulness of it;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"

When one writes this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, and correctly contemplates it, someone may come and praise the gods of the Four Great Kings, praise the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmā heavens, and even up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception; they may praise the first dhyāna and even up to the meditative attainment of neither perception nor non-perception.
He spoke these words: "Good son!

The enjoyment of the pleasures of the five desires within the desire realm, the enjoyment of the bliss of meditative rebirth within the form realm, and the enjoyment of the bliss of quiescence within the formless realm—all these things are likewise impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self; they possess the characteristics of transformation, exhaustion, dispersion, separation, and cessation."

Why do you not, within this very body, realize the fruit of a srotāpanna, the fruit of a sakṛdāgāmin, the fruit of an anāgāmin, the fruit of an arhat, or the path of a pratyekabuddha? Why must you seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi by undergoing various sufferings within the cycle of birth and death in this world?
"When these two do not harmonize, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor even maintain right mindfulness of it;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The Dharma-preacher is alone and free from entanglements, possessing sovereign unimpededness;
yet the Dharma-hearer brings along a large multitude of people.
Because these two are not in harmony, they are unable to write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness. You should know that this is the work of Māra.
The listener has no burdens on their person and is free and unimpeded;
the speaker leads a large multitude of people.
Because these two are not in harmony, they are unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the teacher of the Dharma speaks thus:
'If you can comply with my wishes, I shall give you this Prajñāpāramitā so that you may write it down, read it, recite it, explain it, and correctly bring it to mind.'"
‘If you do not follow my will, I shall not give it to you.

Because the two parties are thus in discord, they are unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor to read, recite, explain, or correctly attend to it; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, there may be a listener who wishes to follow [the teaching] according to their own inclination,
yet the speaker of the Dharma does not permit it.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If the teacher of the Dharma, for the sake of seeking wealth and profit, provides the Prajñāpāramitā for copying, upholding, and even for correct recollection;
yet the listener of the Dharma, because of these causes and conditions, does not wish to receive it from him.
When the two parties do not reach an agreement, such that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* cannot be written down or even correctly recollected, one should know this to be the work of Māra.
It may be that the listener desires to write, read, recite, and explain the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of wealth and profit,
while the speaker, for those same reasons, is unwilling to give it.
"When two people do not harmonize, they will be unable to write down, read, recite, or explain the profound *prajñāpāramitā*;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
If the teacher of the Dharma wishes to go to another region where life is in danger,
but the listener of the Dharma does not wish to follow him,
and because these two are not in harmony, they are unable to write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness of it, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
If the listener wishes to go to another region where life is in danger,
while the teacher of the Dharma does not wish to go,
and the two do not reach an agreement, such that they cannot write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness of it, you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, suppose the teacher of the Dharma wishes to go to another region that is afflicted by famine, high grain prices, and a lack of water,
while the listener of the Dharma does not wish to go along with him."
When the two do not harmonize, such that they are unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness of it, one should know this to be the work of Māra.
It may also be that the listener wishes to go to another region where there is famine, high grain prices, and a lack of water,
while the teacher of the Dharma does not wish to go.
"When the two are not in harmony, one will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
The teacher of the Dharma wishes to go to another region that is prosperous and joyful;
the listener of the Dharma wishes to follow him there.
The teacher of the Dharma says:
"Good son! You have followed me for the sake of gain and offerings; you should reflect well upon this for yourself.
Whether you obtain them or not, do not let yourself regret it later."
Because of these minor causes and conditions, the two are not in harmony.
When the listener hears this, their mind becomes weary, and they think:
"This is a rejection; he does not wish to associate with me."
He will then immediately stop and not go.
Because the two do not harmonize, he will be unable to write the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, suppose the teacher of the Dharma wishes to cross a wilderness, fearing bandits, outcasts, hunters, and fierce beasts or venomous snakes; meanwhile,
the listener of the Dharma wishes to follow after him."
The preacher of the Dharma said:
"Good son! Why would you go there?
Within that place there are many fears, from the fear of bandits to the fear of venomous snakes."

When those who listen to the Dharma hear this, they will know that he does not wish to write down, uphold, or even correctly contemplate the *prajñāpāramitā*; their minds will become weary, and they will have no desire to follow him.
Because of these minor causes and conditions, the two will not be in harmony; you should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, the one who preaches the Dharma may have many donors who frequently visit to inquire after his well-being. For this reason, he says to the listener of the Dharma:
"I have a matter to attend to and must go there.
When those who wish to hear the Dharma perceive this intention, they stop him and do not go.
Because the two parties are thus out of harmony, they are unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness; you should know that this is the work of Māra.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! Māra, the Evil One, will come in the guise of a bhikṣu and employ skillful means to destroy the Prajñāpāramitā, so that it may not be written down, upheld, recited, read, or correctly contemplated."
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,

for what cause and condition does Māra, the Evil One, assume the form of a bhikṣu and employ skillful means to destroy the *prajñāpāramitā*, so that it may not be written down, upheld, or even correctly recollected?"
The Buddha said:
"An evil Māra may come in the form of a bhikṣu to corrupt the minds of good sons and good daughters, causing them to distance themselves from the Prajñāpāramitā."
They will speak thus:
"The sūtras as I have preached them are themselves the Prajñāpāramitā; this sūtra is not the Prajñāpāramitā. Subhūti!
In this regard, when those bhikṣus are being subverted, bodhisattvas who have not yet received their prediction fall into doubt.
Because they have fallen into doubt, they do not write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor do they receive it, uphold it, or even apply correct mindfulness toward it.
"When the two do not harmonize, one will be unable to complete the transcription of the *Prajñāpāramitā* up to its correct recollection;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
A māra, assuming the form of a bhikṣu, approaches the bodhisattva and speaks thus:

"If a bodhisattva practices the prajñāpāramitā, he realizes the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) and attains the fruit of a srotāpanna, the fruit of a sakṛdāgāmin, the fruit of an anāgāmin, the fruit of an arhat, and the path of a pratyekabuddha."
"Because of this lack of harmony, they will be unable to write down the Prajñāpāramitā, nor even maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti!"
When this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being taught, many demonic activities arise; that which hinders the *prajñāpāramitā* constitutes such demonic activity.
A bodhisattva-mahāsattva should recognize them, and having recognized them, should remain far removed from them.
Subhūti said: “World-Honored One!
What are the demonic deeds and obstacles that a bodhisattva should recognize, and having recognized them, should distance himself from?”
The Buddha said:

"Māra-like deeds arise that resemble the *prajñāpāramitā*; Māra-like deeds arise that resemble the *dhyānapāramitā*, the *vīryapāramitā*, the *kṣāntipāramitā*, the *śīlapāramitā*, and the *dānapāramitā*."
A bodhisattva should recognize this, and having recognized it,
should distance himself from it. Furthermore, Subhūti,
those sūtras that are to be practiced by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas— these a bodhisattva mahāsattva should recognize as the work of Māra and distance himself from them.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! By means of internal emptiness, external emptiness, up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence; by means of the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path; and by means of the gates of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—one attains the fruit of a stream-enterer, the fruit of a once-returner, the fruit of a non-returner, the fruit of an arhat, and the path of a pratyekabuddha."
In such sutras as these, Māra assumes the form of a bhikṣu and employs skillful means to provide them to bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Because of this lack of harmony, they will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even to maintain right mindfulness; one should know that this is the work of Māra.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, a wicked Māra may manifest in the form of a Buddha, golden in color and with a fathom-wide radiance, and approach the bodhisattva; that bodhisattva then becomes attached to it.
Because of the causes and conditions of this attachment, their *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) is diminished."
Because of this lack of harmony, one will be unable to write out the Prajñāpāramitā, nor even to maintain right mindfulness;
you should know that this is the work of Māra. "Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a māra manifests in the form of a Buddha or a community of bhikṣus and approaches the bodhisattva, that bodhisattva gives rise to a mind of craving and attachment, thinking:
"In a future life, I too shall be like this."

When a bhikṣu-saṃgha preaches the Dharma for him, because this bodhisattva is greedily attached to the body of Māra, his omniscience (sarvajñatā) diminishes and he is unable to write out the Prajñāpāramitā; one should know that this is the work of Māra.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One may manifest as hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas, practicing the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom, and point them out to good sons and good daughters."

When good sons or good daughters, having seen it, become greedily attached to it, they diminish their *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) because of that attachment; they will be unable to write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor even maintain right mindfulness of it. One should know that this is the work of Māra.

Why is this? Because within this profound Prajñāpāramitā, there is no form, no sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; and so on, up to and including no unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Subhūti! If this Prajñāpāramitā were without form, up to and including without anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, then within it there would be no Buddha, no śrāvaka, no pratyekabuddha, and no bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are empty of intrinsic nature. Furthermore, Subhūti!
When good sons and good daughters write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and when they receive, read, recite, explain, and correctly contemplate it, many obstacles will arise.
Subhūti! For example, within Jambudvīpa, treasures such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musāragalva, agate, and coral are fraught with many hardships and many thieves.
Thus it is, Subhūti! When good sons and good daughters write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, or even when they correctly bring it to mind, many thieves and many obstacles will arise.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is so, World-Honored One!
Within Jambudvīpa, treasures such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musāragalva, agate, and coral are beset by many thieves and many perils.”
"Bhagavān! Sons of good family and daughters of good family are likewise;
when they write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* or even maintain right mindfulness of it, many obstacles arise and many demonic activities (*mārakarman*) occur."

Why is this? Because these foolish people are incited by Māra; when good sons and good daughters write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, or even practice right mindfulness of it, [the fools] will destroy it and cause them to distance themselves from it.
"World-Honored One!

These foolish people possess little knowledge and little wisdom; when these good sons and good daughters write out the profound Prajñāpāramitā, or even when they correctly recollect it, they destroy it and cause them to distance themselves from it."

These foolish people do not delight their minds in the Great Dharma; for this reason, they do not write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, nor do they accept, read, recite, correctly attend to, or practice according to its teaching. Furthermore, they cause others to be ruined so that they too may not write down the profound *prajñāpāramitā* up to practicing according to its teaching.
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is, Subhūti!"

Good sons and good daughters who have newly resolved upon the Mahāyāna, being instigated by Māra, fail to plant roots of goodness, fail to make offerings to the Buddhas, and do not follow spiritual friends; consequently, they do not write out the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and so forth, up to failing to maintain correct mindfulness, thereby creating obstacles.

These sons and daughters of good family possess little wisdom and little insight, and their minds do not delight in the Great Dharma; for this reason, they are unable to write out this profound Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including its correct recollection, because the work of Māra has arisen.

Subhūti! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family is able to write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and even maintain right mindfulness of it, then no works of Māra will arise; they will be able to fulfill the *dhyānapāramitā* up to the *dānapāramitā*, and they will be able to fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness up to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Subhūti, you should know that it is by the power of the Buddha that these sons and daughters of good family are able to write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and even maintain right mindfulness of it; they are also able to fulfill the *dhyānapāramitā* up to the *dānapāramitā*, to fulfill internal emptiness up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), to fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path, and [to fulfill] the ten powers of a Buddha up to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Subhūti! The present Buddhas of the ten directions, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable in number, also assist these sons and daughters of good family, enabling them to write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā and even to maintain it with correct mindfulness.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are irreversible (avaivartika) in the ten directions likewise protect, guard, and assist these good men and good women who write out the profound Prajñāpāramitā, up to and including its correct recollection.
Chapter 48: The Mother of Buddhas. From the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Forty-Eight, "The Mother of Buddhas. The Buddha addressed Subhūti:
"Suppose, for example, there were a woman who had children—perhaps five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, or a thousand."
When the mother falls ill, the sons each diligently seek medical treatment for her.
They think to themselves:

"How can we ensure our mother remains at ease, free from all suffering, affliction, and unpleasant things? That wind, cold, heat, mosquitoes, gadflies, snakes, or vipers should invade her body is a source of anxiety for us."
Those sons constantly sought articles of pleasure to offer to their mother.
Why was this? Because she gave birth to us and showed us the world.
Thus it is, Subhūti! The Buddha constantly beholds this profound Prajñāpāramitā with his Buddha-eye. Why is this?
This profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal the characteristics of the world.
The Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions also constantly behold this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with their Buddha-eyes.
Why is this? Because this profound *prajñāpāramitā* can give birth to all Buddhas, can bestow upon all Buddhas their omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), and can reveal the characteristics of the world.
For this reason, the Buddhas always behold this profound *prajñāpāramitā* with their Buddha-eye.

Furthermore, it is because the *prajñāpāramitā* can give rise to the *dhyānapāramitā* and so forth, up to the *dānapāramitā*; it can give rise to internal emptiness (*adhyātma-śūnyatā*) and so forth, up to the emptiness of non-existence and existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*); it can give rise to the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*) and so forth, up to the eightfold noble path (*āryāṣṭāṅgamārga*); and it can give rise to the ten powers of a Buddha (*buddhabala*) and so forth, up to all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is able to give birth to srotāpannas, sakṛdāgāmins, anāgāmins, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and all Buddhas.

Subhūti! All Buddhas who have already attained, are now attaining, or will attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, all do so by virtue of the causal conditions of profound prajñāpāramitā.

Subhūti! If sons or daughters of good family who seek the path of the Buddha should write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā and even maintain right mindfulness of it, the Buddhas will always regard such persons with their Buddha-eye.

Subhūti! Those sons and daughters of good family who seek the bodhisattva path are constantly protected by the Buddhas of the ten directions, so that they do not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“As the World-Honored One has said, the Prajñāpāramitā can give birth to all Buddhas and can reveal the characteristics of the world.”
World-Honored One!
How is it that the Prajñāpāramitā can give birth to all Buddhas?
How is it that it can reveal the characteristics of the world?
"How is it that all Buddhas are born from the perfection of wisdom?
How is it that all Buddhas teach the characteristics of the world? The Buddha told Subhūti:
“It is from within this profound *prajñāpāramitā* that the ten powers of a Buddha, up to the eighteen unique qualities and all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), are produced. Subhūti!...”
Because one attains these causes and conditions for all dharmas, one is called a Buddha. Subhūti!
For this reason, the profound Prajñāpāramitā is able to give birth to all Buddhas.
“Subhūti! The Buddhas have taught that the five aggregates are the characteristics of the world. Subhūti said:
“World-Honored One!
How does the profound *prajñāpāramitā* explain the characteristics of the five aggregates?
How does the profound *prajñāpāramitā* reveal the suchness of the five aggregates?”

“Subhūti! The perfection of wisdom does not demonstrate the breaking up of the five aggregates, nor does it demonstrate their destruction; it does not demonstrate arising, nor does it demonstrate cessation; it does not demonstrate defilement, nor does it demonstrate purity; it does not demonstrate increase, nor does it demonstrate decrease; it does not demonstrate entering, nor does it demonstrate exiting; it does not demonstrate the past, nor does it demonstrate the future, nor does it demonstrate the present.”

Why is this? Because the characteristic of emptiness is neither broken nor destroyed; the characteristic of signlessness and the characteristic of wishlessness are neither broken nor destroyed. Thus it is shown that the dharma of non-arising, the dharma of non-birth, the dharma of non-existence, and the dharma of nature possess such unbreakable and indestructible characteristics.
Thus it is, Subhūti! The Buddha has said that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can reveal the characteristics of the world. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
By means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddhas fully know the mental activities of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings.

Subhūti, within this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, there are no sentient beings and no name for "sentient beings"; there is no form and no name for "form"; there is no feeling, perception, formation, or consciousness, and no names for "feeling, perception, formation, or consciousness. There is no eye up to no mind; no eye-consciousness up to no mind-consciousness; no eye-contact up to no mind-contact; and so on, up to no all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and no name for "all-knowledge."
Thus it is, Subhūti! This profound perfection of wisdom can reveal the characteristics of the world. Subhūti!

This profound Prajñāpāramitā does not indicate form, nor does it indicate feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, and so on, up to not indicating the knowledge of all modes. Why is this?
Subhūti! Within this profound prajñāpāramitā, even prajñāpāramitā itself does not exist; how much less so form, up to and including all-knowledge?
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

As for all sentient beings, whether they have form or are formless, whether they possess perception or lack perception, whether they possess neither perception nor non-perception, whether they belong to this world-system or to world-systems throughout the ten directions—whether these sentient beings have concentrated minds or distracted minds—the Buddha knows those concentrated and distracted minds as they truly are."
Subhūti! How does the Buddha know the characteristics of the concentrated mind and the distracted mind of sentient beings?
He knows them by means of the characteristic of dharmas.
By what characteristic of dharmas is this known? Subhūti, within these characteristics of dharmas,
there is not even the characteristic of the characteristic of dharmas, let alone the existence of a concentrated mind or a distracted mind.
Subhūti! By means of these characteristics of dharmas, the Buddha knows the concentrated minds and the distracted minds of sentient beings. Furthermore, Subhūti!
The Buddha knows the concentrated minds and the distracted minds of sentient beings. How does he know them? Subhūti!

One knows it by way of the characteristic of exhaustion; one knows it by way of the characteristic of non-defilement; one knows it by way of the characteristic of cessation; one knows it by way of the characteristic of abandonment; one knows it by way of the characteristic of tranquility; and one knows it by way of the characteristic of detachment.
Thus it is, Subhūti! By means of the prajñāpāramitā, the Buddha knows the concentrated minds and the distracted minds of sentient beings. "Furthermore, Subhūti!"
By means of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Buddha knows the defiled minds of sentient beings; he knows the defiled mind as it truly is, and he knows the hateful mind and the deluded mind as they truly are.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does the Buddha know the defiled minds of sentient beings, knowing them as they truly are?”
"How does one know a mind of anger and a mind of delusion as they truly are?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"In the true mark of a defiled mind, there is no mark of a defiled mind."

Why is this? Because in the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), even the mind and mental factors (*citta-caitasika-dharma*) cannot be apprehended; how much less, then, can one apprehend a defiled mind or an undefiled mind? Subhūti!
In the true mark (*lakṣaṇa*) of anger and delusion, there is neither the state of anger nor the state of delusion. Why is this?

Because in the true mark, even the mind and mental factors (*citta-caitasika-dharma*) cannot be apprehended; how much less can one apprehend a state of anger or non-anger, or a state of delusion or non-delusion?

In this way, Subhūti, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha knows a defiled mind of sentient beings as it truly is—a defiled mind; he knows a mind of hatred and a mind of delusion as they truly are—a mind of hatred and a mind of delusion.

"Furthermore, Subhūti! By means of the perfection of wisdom, the Buddha knows, as it truly is, that sentient beings have minds free from defilement; he knows, as it truly is, that they have minds free from hatred and minds free from delusion."
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
how does one truly know, as it really is, that a sentient being’s mind is unstained when it is unstained?”
"How does one truly know a mind free from hatred as a mind free from hatred?
How does one truly know a mind free from delusion as a mind free from delusion?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“Within this mind that has no characteristic of defilement, neither the characteristic of defilement nor the characteristic of non-defilement can be apprehended.
Why is this? Subhūti!”
Because two minds do not coexist.
Thus, Subhūti, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha knows a mind that is undefiled as it truly is: an undefiled mind.
Subhūti! Within these characteristics of a mind free from hatred and a mind free from delusion, neither a deluded mind nor a non-deluded mind can be apprehended. Why is this?
Because two minds do not coexist.
Thus, Subhūti, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*,
the Buddha knows truly that sentient beings possess neither a mind of hatred nor a mind of delusion.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha knows the expansive mind of these sentient beings as it truly is: 'This is an expansive mind.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that the Buddha, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, knows the expansive mind of these sentient beings as an expansive mind, in accordance with reality? “Subhūti!

The Buddha knows that the characteristics of the minds of all sentient beings are neither broad nor narrow, neither increasing nor decreasing, neither coming nor going, because the characteristics of the mind are detached from such qualities.
Thus, this mind is neither broad nor narrow, and so on, up to neither coming nor going.
Why is this? Because the nature of the mind does not exist.
Who creates the vast, who creates the narrow, and so forth, up to coming and going?
Thus it is, Subhūti! By means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha knows the expansive mind of these sentient beings as an expansive mind, in accordance with reality. Furthermore, Subhūti!
“By means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha knows the great minds of these sentient beings as they truly are—namely, that they are great minds.
Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"How does the Buddha, by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, truly know the great mind of these sentient beings as a great mind?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"By means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddha does not perceive a coming or going characteristic of the minds of sentient beings; he does not perceive a characteristic of arising, a characteristic of ceasing, or a characteristic of abiding and changing in the minds of sentient beings."
Why is this? Because these mental natures are non-existent, who comes and who goes, who is born, ceases, abides, or changes? Thus it is, Subhūti!
